In Reykjavík there are many heated outdoor pools where you can swim outside even in winter.

teile.einleitung: The Provence is a region in the south-east of France on the Mediterranean. It is famous for lavender fields, plenty of sunshine, old towns and varied nature. Through the middle of the area flows the Rhône, which rises in Switzerland.
wichtigste: The Provence lies in the south-east of France on the Mediterranean.
In summer violet lavender plants bloom in many fields.
In the 14th century the popes lived in Avignon.
Marseille was founded by Greeks around 600 BC.
The mistral is a cold, strong north wind.
In the Camargue live flamingos and white horses.

abschnitte.text: The **Provence** has a **Mediterranean climate** with hot, dry summers and mild winters. In summer **lavender fields** colour many plateaus violet, for example the **Valensole** plateau. From the flowers a fragrant oil is obtained for soaps and perfumes. Olives, vines and many herbs also grow here, known as **herbes de Provence**.

Around 600 BC **Greeks** from Phocaea founded the city of **Massalia**, today's **Marseille**. It is regarded as the oldest city in France. Later the Romans ruled here. In Arles a Roman amphitheatre still stands today. From 1309 to 1377 the **popes** lived not in Rome but in **Avignon**. The mighty **Palace of the Popes** recalls this.

The **mistral** is a cold, strong wind from the north. It blows through the valley of the **Rhône** to the Mediterranean. Often it brings clear, sunny but cool weather. The Rhône rises at the Rhône Glacier in the **Valais**, flows through Lake Geneva and reaches the sea in the Provence.

Between the arms of the mouth of the Rhône lies the **Camargue**. This is a flat area with lagoons, marshes and pastures. In the lagoons live many pink **flamingos**. On the pastures roam semi-wild **white horses** and black bulls. Rice is also grown here and sea salt is extracted.

The River Verdon has carved the **Gorges du Verdon**, a gorge up to about 700 metres deep with turquoise water. It is regarded as one of the largest gorges in Europe. In the north stands **Mont Ventoux**, about 1900 metres high. Because it rises free above the landscape and its summit is pale and bare, it is called the **Giant of Provence**. In the Tour de France it is a famous climb.

gewusst: Water from Lake Geneva flows by way of the Rhône as far as the Camargue.
The painter Vincent van Gogh painted many of his best-known pictures in Arles.

teile.einleitung: Pula is a port city in the south of the Istrian peninsula in Croatia. The city is over 2000 years old. It is famous above all for its large Roman amphitheatre, the Arena.
wichtigste: Pula lies in the south of the Istrian peninsula in Croatia.
The Arena of Pula was built in the 1st century AD.
It is among the best preserved amphitheatres in the world.
Today concerts and a film festival take place in the Arena.
In Croatia people have paid with the euro since 2023.

abschnitte.text: An **amphitheatre** is an oval building with rows of seats around a space in the middle. The Romans watched contests and shows there. The **Arena of Pula** was built in the **1st century AD**. Its outer wall of pale limestone still stands almost completely. This makes it one of the best preserved amphitheatres in the world.

Pula was already an important city in the time of the **Romans**. Besides the Arena there are other Roman buildings, such as a triumphal arch and a temple for Emperor **Augustus**. Later Pula belonged to Venice and to Austria. Under Austria the city became a large port for the navy and a shipyard.

Today Pula is a popular holiday town by the sea. In summer **concerts** and the **Pula Film Festival** take place in the Arena, and thousands of people sit on the old stone steps. Nearby lies the **Brijuni** National Park, a group of islands. Many holidaymakers from Switzerland also travel to Istria.

gewusst: The Arena of Pula once had room for several thousand spectators.
The Arena is almost 2000 years old and is still used for events.

teile.einleitung: Wales is one of the four countries of the United Kingdom. It lies in the west of the island of Great Britain and has a language of its own, Welsh. Wales is known for castles, sheep, rugby and the red dragon.
wichtigste: The capital of Wales is Cardiff.
The flag shows a red dragon on green and white.
Many people speak Welsh as well as English.
The highest mountain is Snowdon at 1,085 metres.
There are more than 600 castles in Wales.
Rugby is the most popular sport.
The heir to the throne usually bears the title Prince of Wales.

abschnitte.text: On the flag of Wales you can see a **red dragon** on a green and white background. It is the emblem of the country. Another old symbol is the **leek**. On the national day, St David’s Day on 1 March, some people pin on a leek or a daffodil. The capital and largest city is **Cardiff** in the south by the sea.

In Wales people speak **English** and **Welsh**. Welsh is a very old Celtic language. Place signs and signposts are often labelled in **both languages**. On the island of **Anglesey** lies a village with one of the longest place names in Europe: **Llanfairpwllgwyngyll**. The full name has 58 letters and describes the location of the church.

Wales is known for its **castles**, of which there are more than 600. Some are more than 700 years old, for example the castles of **Caernarfon** and **Conwy**. The highest mountain is **Snowdon**, in Welsh **Yr Wyddfa**, at 1,085 metres. It lies in Snowdonia National Park in the north. On the green meadows live far more **sheep** than people, as Wales has only about 3 million inhabitants.

The most popular sport in Wales is **rugby**. Matches of the national team are great festivals with a lot of singing. The eldest son and heir to the throne of the British monarch traditionally receives the title **Prince of Wales**. Since 2022 it has been held by **Prince William**. Wales also has its own parliament, which decides some matters itself.

gewusst: The long place name on Anglesey is so famous that travellers like to have their photo taken with the station sign.
Snowdon is called Yr Wyddfa in Welsh.

teile.einleitung: Lake Bohinj, called Wocheiner See in German, is the largest permanent natural lake in Slovenia. It lies in the Julian Alps in Triglav National Park. The water is cold and very clear.
wichtigste: Lake Bohinj is the largest permanent natural lake in Slovenia.
In German it is called the Wocheiner See.
It lies in Triglav National Park in the Julian Alps.
The lake was shaped by glaciers.
Only Lake Cerknica can grow larger in high water, but it dries out at times.

abschnitte.text: **Lake Bohinj** lies in the **Julian Alps** in the north-west of **Slovenia**. It belongs to **Triglav National Park**, the only national park in the country. The lake is surrounded by high mountains. It was shaped by **glaciers** in the Ice Age. Its water is cold and very **clear**.

Lake Bohinj is the **largest permanent natural lake** in Slovenia. **Lake Cerknica** can grow larger in high water. But it dries out completely at times, because the water seeps away into the limestone ground. Lake Bohinj is fed by streams, for example by the **Savica** waterfall. The **Sava** flows out of the lake, an important river in Slovenia.

On the shore stands an old **church** with a stone bridge. In summer many people swim, hike and paddle on the lake. In winter you can go **skiing** nearby. The lake is quieter than the better-known **Lake Bled** close by. Above the area rises **Triglav**, the highest mountain in Slovenia.

gewusst: Triglav, the mountain above the national park, even appears on the flag of Slovenia.

teile.einleitung: Slavonia is a flat, fertile region in the east of Croatia. It lies between the rivers Drava, Sava and Danube. The largest city is Osijek.
wichtigste: Slavonia lies in the east of Croatia.
The region is flat and very fertile.
The largest city is Osijek on the Drava.
The Drava flows in the north, the Sava in the south and the Danube in the east.
Slavonia is known for agriculture and oak forests.

abschnitte.text: Slavonia lies in the **east of Croatia**. In the north the **Drava** borders the region, in the south the **Sava** and in the east the **Danube**. Beyond the borders lie Hungary, Serbia and Bosnia and Herzegovina. Slavonia is part of the great **Pannonian Plain** and is therefore mostly flat.

The soil in Slavonia is very **fertile**. On the wide fields grow wheat, maize, sugar beet and sunflowers. That is why Slavonia is often called the breadbasket of Croatia. There are also vineyards and large **oak forests**. The oak wood is used, for example, to make wine barrels.

The largest city is **Osijek** on the Drava. It has an old fortress town, the **Tvrđa**. Other towns are Vukovar on the Danube and Slavonski Brod on the Sava. Slavonia is also known for **kulen**, a spicy sausage made with paprika.

gewusst: Near Osijek lies the Kopački Rit nature reserve, a large wetland with many birds.

teile.einleitung: The Sami are an indigenous people who have lived in the north of Europe for a very long time. Their homeland Sápmi stretches across Norway, Sweden, Finland and Russia. Today they are fighting to preserve their languages, their culture and their way of life.
wichtigste: The Sami are the only recognised indigenous people in the EU.
The Sami languages belong to the Uralic languages.
North Sami has the most speakers.
The traditional costume is called the gákti.
Reindeer herding is culturally very important for many Sami.
The Norwegian Sámi Parliament has its seat in Karasjok.
With “Norwegianisation”, Sami culture was suppressed for a long time.

abschnitte.text: **Indigenous** is the word for peoples who were already living in an area before today’s states came into being. The Sami live in **Sápmi**, the north of Norway, Sweden, Finland and the Russian Kola Peninsula. Because Sweden and Finland belong to the European Union, the Sami are the **only recognised indigenous people in the EU**. How many Sami there are is hard to say, and estimates differ widely. Most Sami live in Norway.

The **Sami languages** belong to the **Uralic languages** and are distantly related to Finnish and Hungarian. There are several Sami languages, some of which differ greatly from one another. **North Sami** has the most speakers. Some smaller Sami languages are now spoken by only a few people. Today there are Sami schools, newspapers, radio and television.

For many Sami, **reindeer herding** is still particularly important culturally, even though only some of them live from it. The herds move back and forth between summer and winter pastures. At festivals many Sami wear their traditional costume, the **gákti**. Colours and patterns often show which area someone comes from. The **joik** is also well known, a Sami song used to remember people, animals or places.

For a long time states tried to make the Sami fit in with the majority. In Norway this policy is called **Norwegianisation**: children often were not allowed to speak Sami at school. Later this changed. In **1990** **Norway** became the first country to ratify **ILO Convention 169** on the rights of indigenous peoples. The Norwegian **Sámi Parliament** (Sameting), an elected body representing the Sami, has its seat in **Karasjok**.

Today there are conflicts when mines, roads or **wind farms** are built on the reindeer’s grazing land. The dispute over wind farms on the **Fosen** peninsula in Norway is well known. In 2021 the Supreme Court of Norway ruled that the rights of Sami reindeer herders had been violated there. The case shows that climate protection and the rights of indigenous peoples can sometimes come into conflict. Those involved are looking for solutions.

gewusst: The Sami languages are distantly related to Finnish and Hungarian.
A joik is often not a song about someone, but is meant to represent the person or place itself.

teile.einleitung: The Salzkammergut is a region in Austria with many lakes and mountains. It stretches across three federal states and has been shaped for centuries by salt mining. Today it is a popular holiday and day-trip area.
wichtigste: The Salzkammergut lies in Upper Austria, Salzburg and Styria.
It gets its name from salt.
Lake Attersee is the largest lake that lies entirely in Austria.
Bad Ischl was the summer residence of Emperor Franz Joseph.
On Lake Wolfgangsee lies St Wolfgang with the “White Horse Inn” hotel.
Hallstatt is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

abschnitte.text: In the Salzkammergut, **salt** has been taken from the mountain for thousands of years. In the past the salt mines belonged to the ruler of the land. His administration was called the **Kammer**, so the area was called the **Kammergut**. The state earned a lot of money from salt. Today the region stretches across the three federal states of **Upper Austria**, **Salzburg** and **Styria**.

In the Salzkammergut many clear lakes lie between steep mountains. **Lake Attersee** is the **largest lake that lies entirely in Austria**. Lake Traunsee, Lake Mondsee, Lake Hallstatt and **Lake Wolfgangsee** are also well known. In the south rises the **Dachstein massif** with glaciers and caves. In summer many people swim, sail and hike here.

The spa town of **Bad Ischl** was the **summer residence** of Emperor **Franz Joseph** for decades. He spent many summers in the Kaiservilla and liked to go hunting. In **St Wolfgang** on Lake Wolfgangsee stands the hotel **“Im Weissen Rössl”** (“The White Horse Inn”). It became famous through a funny operetta from 1930 that is set there. In **2024** Bad Ischl, together with the region, was a **European Capital of Culture**.

The little village of **Hallstatt** lies tightly squeezed between lake and mountain. Its salt mine is considered one of the oldest in the world. Based on finds from graves near Hallstatt, a whole period of prehistory has even been named, the **Hallstatt period**. The Hallstatt and Dachstein region is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**. Today so many visitors come that the village has to manage the flow of tourists.

gewusst: A whole period of the Iron Age is named after the village of Hallstatt, the Hallstatt period.
Emperor Franz Joseph spent many summers in Bad Ischl.

teile.einleitung: The sirocco is a warm wind that blows from North Africa across the Mediterranean to southern Europe. It often brings muggy air, rain or Saharan dust. Sometimes you can even see its traces on the snow in the Swiss Alps.
wichtigste: The sirocco is a warm wind from North Africa.
It arises when low-pressure systems move eastwards over the Mediterranean.
Over the sea it picks up moisture and becomes muggy.
On the Croatian coast it is called the jugo.
In Venice it can make the flooding called acqua alta worse.
It sometimes carries Saharan dust as far as the Alps.
It blows most often in March and November.

abschnitte.text: The **sirocco** comes from the **Sahara** and usually blows from the south-east or south. It is set off by **low-pressure areas** that move east over the Mediterranean. On their front side they draw warm desert air northwards. The sirocco blows most often in **March** and in **November**. The name goes back to an **Arabic word for east**.

In North Africa the sirocco is hot, dry and dusty. On its way across the **Mediterranean** it picks up a lot of **moisture**. That is why in **southern Italy** and on Sicily it is usually **damp and muggy**. Many people feel tired and irritable when the sirocco blows. On the Croatian Adriatic coast the wind is called the **jugo**, which means south.

The sirocco blows across the whole Adriatic to the north-west. In doing so it **pushes** water into the northern Adriatic. If the high tide comes on top of that, the water rises sharply in **Venice**. This flooding is called **acqua alta**. Then St Mark’s Square and many lanes are under water, and people walk on raised wooden walkways.

The sirocco can carry fine **Saharan sand** high into the air. If this falls with the rain, the rain turns reddish. In southern Italy this is called **blood rain**. After such weather situations you can sometimes also see a **yellowish-red layer of dust** on the snow in the **Swiss Alps**. The sky can then look milky yellow, and fine dust is left on cars.

gewusst: In Egypt a similar hot desert wind is called “khamsin”, which means “fifty”.
Saharan dust from Africa can be blown as far as the Swiss glaciers.

teile.einleitung: The Leaning Tower of Pisa is one of the most famous towers in the world. It stands in the city of Pisa in Italy and is well known because it clearly leans to one side. It is actually the bell tower of Pisa Cathedral.
wichtigste: The tower of Pisa is famous because it leans.
It leans because the ground beneath it is too soft.
It was built as a bell tower for the cathedral.
Seven bells hang in the tower.
The tower is about 56 metres high.
Experts have secured it so that it does not fall over.
It stands on the Piazza dei Miracoli, the Square of Miracles.

abschnitte.text: The **Leaning Tower of Pisa** stands in the city of **Pisa** in Tuscany. It was built as the **bell tower**, in Italian the **campanile**, of the cathedral. **Seven bells** hang at the top. The tower is about **56 metres** high and made of white marble. It has several storeys with colonnades, and almost 300 steps lead to the top.

Building began in **1173**. After only a few storeys the tower began to lean. The reason is the **soft ground** of clay and sand, which gave way on one side. Because of wars, building work was interrupted for long periods several times. The builders tried to make up for the lean and built the upper storeys slightly curved. The tower was only finished after about 200 years.

Over the centuries the tower leaned more and more. In 1990 it was closed to visitors because there was a danger of collapse. **Experts** then **secured** it: among other things, they carefully removed soil from under the higher side so that it leaned back a little. Since 2001 you can climb it again. It is still leaning, but much more stable than before.

The tower stands on the **Piazza dei Miracoli**, the **Square of Miracles**. The cathedral, the baptistery and an old cemetery stand there too, all in pale marble. The square is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**. Many tourists take a funny **photo**: they stand so that it looks as if they are **holding up** the tower with their hands. A well-known story says that Galileo Galilei dropped balls from the tower, but whether that is true is not certain.

gewusst: The upper storeys were built slightly curved because the builders wanted to make up for the lean.
The tower was closed from 1990 to 2001 so that it could be secured.

teile.einleitung: A polder is low-lying land surrounded by dykes. To keep it dry, the water has to be pumped out all the time. The Netherlands are especially well known for polders.
wichtigste: A polder is land enclosed by dykes with an artificially regulated water level.
Many polders in the Netherlands lie below sea level.
In the past windmills pumped the water out, today electric pumps and diesel pumps do.
The province of Flevoland was laid out almost entirely on drained land.
Schiphol Airport lies on the bed of a former lake.
The lowest point in the Netherlands lies about 7 metres below sea level.

abschnitte.text: A **polder** is an area surrounded by **dykes**, that is, by long earth embankments against the water. Often there used to be a lake, a marsh or even sea there. The water in the ditches of the polder does not run off by itself, because the land lies too low. So it is pumped over the dyke into canals at a higher level. Without dykes and pumps many polders would be under water at once.

In the past **windmills** drove scoop wheels or screws that lifted the water upwards. The 19 mills of **Kinderdijk** near Rotterdam, built around 1740, are famous. Since 1997 they have been a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Later came steam pumps. The **Woudagemaal** in Friesland opened in 1920 and is the largest steam pumping station in the world that is still working. It too is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

In the 19th century the large lake **Haarlemmermeer** was drained with steam pumps. Today **Schiphol** Airport lies there, a few metres below sea level. The lowest point in the country lies in the **Zuidplaspolder** near Rotterdam, about 6.7 metres below sea level.

In the 20th century the **Zuiderzee**, an arm of the sea, was dammed off. New polders arose in it. The **Flevopolder** covers about 970 square kilometres and is surrounded by water on all sides. It is regarded as the largest artificial island in the world. From these polders **Flevoland** was formed in 1986, the twelfth province of the Netherlands.

On the German North Sea coast too there is land enclosed by dykes. In Schleswig-Holstein it is called a **Koog**, and in Lower Saxony also a **Groden**. In Switzerland no land lies below sea level. But marshes were drained here too, for example the **Grosses Moos** in the Seeland through the Jura Waters Correction.

gewusst: A large part of the Netherlands lies below sea level and is protected by dykes.
The Dutch say: “God created the world, but the Dutch created the Netherlands.”

teile.einleitung: Stonehenge is one of the most famous stone monuments in the world. It stands in the south of England and was built by people of the Stone Age. Researchers are still puzzling over how they moved the huge stones.
wichtigste: Stonehenge stands on Salisbury Plain in the county of Wiltshire in England.
People of the Stone Age built it without machines, in several phases over many centuries.
The large sarsen stones of hard sandstone each weigh about 25 tonnes.
The smaller bluestones mostly come from the Preseli Hills in Wales.
On the longest day of the year the sun rises over a particular stone.
Stonehenge has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1986.

abschnitte.text: Stonehenge consists of large stones arranged in circles and arcs. On the outside there once stood a circle of upright stones with capstones on top. Inside, five especially large **trilithons** form a horseshoe. A trilithon consists of three stones: two uprights and a capstone laid across them. Many stones have fallen over in the course of time or are missing today.

The English word **henge** describes a round structure from the Neolithic. It is surrounded by an earth bank and a ditch. Stonehenge also has such a circular ditch, which is one of the oldest parts of the site. It was dug long before the large stones. The name Stonehenge therefore means roughly “henge made of stone”.

The large **sarsen stones** are made of a very hard sandstone. They come from the area around Marlborough, about 25 kilometres to the north. The smaller **bluestones** mostly come from the Preseli Hills in Wales, more than 200 kilometres away. How people at that time transported such heavy stones so far is not entirely clear. They probably used wooden sledges, rollers, ropes and a great deal of muscle power.

Stonehenge is aligned with the sun. On the longest day of the year, the **summer solstice**, the sun rises over a particular stone. On the shortest day in winter it sets on the opposite side. That is why many people come every June to see the sunrise. Exactly what Stonehenge was used for is not known for certain. Many experts think of a place for festivals, ceremonies and burials.

In 1986 Stonehenge was added to the **UNESCO World Heritage** list. It includes other Stone Age monuments in the surrounding area, such as the great stone circle of Avebury. Today visitors come from all over the world. To keep the stones protected, you can usually only walk around the circle from some distance.

gewusst: A sarsen stone weighs about as much as several lorries put together.
The bluestones were brought more than 200 kilometres, without wheels made of metal or engines.

teile.einleitung: Planica is a place in an Alpine valley in the north-west of Slovenia. It is world famous for its huge hills for ski flying.
wichtigste: Planica lies in Slovenia in the Julian Alps, near the border with Italy.
One of the largest ski flying hills in the world stands there.
World Cup ski flying events take place in Planica regularly.
Distance world records have been set here several times.
In 1936 a person first jumped over 100 metres here.

abschnitte.text: **Planica** lies in a valley of the **Julian Alps** in the north-west of **Slovenia**, not far from the town of Kranjska Gora. The border with **Italy** is very close. All around the valley steep limestone mountains rise up. In winter there is a lot of snow, and in summer hikers come.

**Ski flying** is ski jumping on especially large hills. The jumpers fly well over 200 metres. In Planica the hill of the **Gorišek brothers** is one of the largest **ski flying hills** in the world. **World Cup ski flying** events take place here regularly, often at the end of the season. Tens of thousands of spectators then cheer the jumpers.

Planica is a place of **distance world records**. As early as **1936** the Austrian Sepp Bradl jumped over **100 metres** here, the first person to do so. Since then many more records have been set in Planica. In 2023 the **Nordic World Ski Championships** were also held here.

gewusst: In a ski flight a jumper is in the air for several seconds.

teile.einleitung: The Cyprus conflict is a dispute over the future of the island of Cyprus. Since 1974 it has been divided into a Greek Cypriot south and a Turkish Cypriot north. So far all attempts at reunification have failed.
wichtigste: In 1960 Cyprus became independent, and Greece, Turkey and Great Britain became guarantor powers.
Enosis means the hoped-for union with Greece.
In 1974 a coup and a Turkish military intervention followed.
The Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus, declared in 1983, is recognised only by Turkey.
In 2004 the Annan Plan failed because the Greek Cypriots rejected it.
In the north EU law is suspended.

abschnitte.text: On Cyprus live **Greek Cypriots** and **Turkish Cypriots**. In the 20th century many Greek Cypriots demanded **enosis**, that is, union with Greece. Turkish Cypriots countered with a demand for **partition**, in Turkish **taksim**. At **independence in 1960**, **Greece**, **Turkey** and **Great Britain** became guarantor powers. A treaty was meant to secure the constitution and independence.

In July **1974** the then military government in Athens supported a **coup** on Cyprus. Its aim was union with Greece. **Turkey** then intervened **militarily**, citing the treaty of guarantee. Since then it has controlled the north. Many people had to leave their homes. The hotel district of **Varosha** near Famagusta was sealed off and stayed empty for decades.

In **1983** the **Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus** was declared in the north. The **UN Security Council** declared this invalid. Only **Turkey** recognises it as a state. Internationally the north counts as part of the Republic of Cyprus. A UN **buffer zone** separates the parts. In 1960 Great Britain also kept the military bases of **Akrotiri** and **Dhekelia** in the south as territories of its own.

In **2004** both communities voted on the UN’s **Annan Plan**. Around 76 per cent of Greek Cypriots rejected it, and around 65 per cent of Turkish Cypriots voted in favour. Because both had to agree, it **failed**. In the same year Cyprus joined the **EU**. In the north, however, EU law is **suspended**, because the government does not control it.

For some years now there have been **crossing points** between the two parts. In 2008 **Ledra Street** in Nicosia became a pedestrian crossing. For decades it had been cut off by barricades. Its opening was seen as a sign of **rapprochement**. Since 2020 parts of Varosha have been open to visitors again, which was criticised internationally. Talks about a solution continue.

gewusst: Nicosia is regarded as the last divided capital in Europe.
The British military bases on Cyprus do not legally belong to the Republic of Cyprus.

teile.einleitung: Serbia is a country in south-eastern Europe on the Balkan Peninsula. It has no access to the sea. The capital Belgrade lies where the Sava flows into the Danube.
wichtigste: Serbia lies on the Balkan Peninsula in south-eastern Europe.
The country has no access to the sea.
The capital is Belgrade.
The Danube flows through Serbia.
Serbia is among the largest raspberry producers in the world.
In Serbia people write in both the Cyrillic and the Latin script.

abschnitte.text: Serbia lies in the middle of the **Balkan Peninsula**. It is surrounded by other countries, including Hungary, Romania, Bulgaria, Croatia and Bosnia and Herzegovina. Serbia has **no access to the sea**, similar to Switzerland. In the north the country is flat and fertile. In the south it becomes more mountainous.

The capital **Belgrade** is one of the oldest cities in Europe. It lies where the **Sava** flows into the **Danube**. Above the river junction stands the old Kalemegdan fortress, now a large park. The Danube is an important waterway for ships. Further east it flows through the narrow **Iron Gates** on the border with Romania.

**Agriculture** is important in Serbia. On the fertile fields in the north, maize, wheat and sunflowers grow. Serbia is especially well known for **raspberries**: the country is among the largest producers in the world. Many raspberries are frozen and sold to other countries. Plums also play a big role.

The official language is **Serbian**. One special feature: Serbian can be written in two scripts, **Cyrillic** and **Latin**. On street signs you often see both. Serbia used to be part of **Yugoslavia**. Many people with roots in Serbia live in Switzerland.

gewusst: Belgrade means “White City” when translated.
The tennis player Novak Đoković comes from Serbia.

teile.einleitung: Trogir is a small town on the coast of Croatia, not far from Split. Its old town lies on a small island and is very well preserved. Since 1997 it has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
wichtigste: Trogir lies in Dalmatia on the Croatian Adriatic coast, near Split.
The old town lies on a small island between the mainland and the island of Čiovo.
Bridges connect the old town with both sides.
The buildings date from many centuries.
Since 1997 the old town has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

abschnitte.text: The old town of **Trogir** lies on a small island. On one side is the mainland, on the other the larger island of **Čiovo**. Bridges connect the old town with both sides. The ancient **Greeks** already founded a settlement here. Later the Romans, among others, and for a long time the Republic of Venice ruled the town.

In the narrow lanes stand churches, palaces and houses from many centuries. Especially well known is the **Cathedral of Saint Lawrence** with an elaborately decorated stone doorway. By the sea stands an old **fortress**. Because so many buildings are well preserved, the old town was added to the **UNESCO World Heritage** list in 1997. Today Trogir is a popular holiday destination.

gewusst: In Trogir you can stroll in a few minutes past buildings from several centuries.

teile.einleitung: The Peloponnese is a large peninsula in the south of Greece. Here lay famous places of antiquity such as Olympia, Sparta and Mycenae.
wichtigste: The Corinth Canal separates the Peloponnese from the rest of the mainland.
The canal opened in 1893.
In Olympia the Olympic Games of antiquity took place.
Sparta was known for its strict training of warriors.
The theatre of Epidaurus has exceptional acoustics.
Nafplio was the capital of Greece until 1834.

abschnitte.text: The name **Peloponnese** means **“island of Pelops”**. “Nesos” means island in Greek, and **Pelops** was a king from legend. The peninsula is joined to the mainland only by a narrow **isthmus** near Corinth. This is cut through by the **Corinth Canal**, which opened in **1893**. It is about 6 kilometres long and very narrow. Since 2004 the **Rio-Antirrio Bridge** has also linked the north-west with the mainland.

In the sanctuary of **Olympia** the **Olympic Games of antiquity** were held in honour of Zeus. The athletes came from the whole Greek world. Even today the **Olympic flame** is lit in Olympia before it is taken to the modern Games.

The city state of **Sparta** was known for its harsh upbringing. Boys from about the age of seven were trained as soldiers. This is where the word **“spartan”** for plain and strict comes from. Even older is the citadel of **Mycenae**. Its main entrance is the **Lion Gate** with two stone lions above the gate.

In **Epidaurus** stands a large **ancient theatre** with over 12,000 seats. It has exceptional **acoustics**. You can hear even a soft word from the stage in the topmost row. To this day performances still take place there in summer.

After liberation from Ottoman rule, **Nafplio** was the **capital** of the young Greek state from 1829 to **1834**. Then the seat of government was moved to **Athens**. Between Sparta and Kalamata rises the **Taygetos** mountain range. At over 2400 metres it is the highest in the Peloponnese.

gewusst: The Corinth Canal was already planned in antiquity, but built only over 2000 years later.
The Rio-Antirrio Bridge is about 2.9 kilometres long and is among the longest cable-stayed bridges in the world.

teile.einleitung: Surtsey is a young volcanic island south of Iceland. It rose out of the water from 1963 during an eruption under the sea. Since then researchers have been observing there how plants and animals settle new land.
wichtigste: Surtsey lies south of Iceland and belongs to the Westman Islands.
The island was formed in a volcanic eruption from 1963 to 1967.
It is named after Surtr, a fire giant from the Norse legends.
Only researchers may enter the island.
Surtsey has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2008.

abschnitte.text: In November 1963 fishermen south of Iceland noticed smoke over the sea. A **volcano** on the sea floor had erupted, and soon new land was poking out of the water. The eruption lasted until 1967. This is how the island of **Surtsey** came into being. Its name comes from **Surtr**, a fire giant from the old Norse legends.

At the beginning Surtsey was just bare rock and ash. Researchers wanted to know how life reaches new land. That is why the island is strictly protected, and only scientists may enter it. They observe how **seeds** arrive with wind, water and birds. Little by little, mosses, flowers, insects and **seabirds** settled. With their droppings the birds bring nutrients that help the plants grow.

Since the end of the eruption, wind and waves have been slowly wearing the island away. Loose ash is washed away especially quickly. Today Surtsey is much smaller than shortly after the eruption. Harder parts of the rock will probably remain for a long time yet. Because of its great value for research, the island was added to the **UNESCO World Heritage** list in 2008.

gewusst: Researchers must take care not to bring any seeds to the island on their shoes or clothes.
Surtsey is younger than many of today’s grandparents.

teile.einleitung: Prizren is an old city in the south of Kosovo. It lies at the foot of the Šar Mountains and is known for its old town with a stone bridge, mosques, churches and a fortress. Many people regard it as the most beautiful city in Kosovo.
wichtigste: Prizren lies in the south of Kosovo at the foot of the Šar Mountains.
An old stone bridge crosses the river in the old town.
Above the city stands a fortress with a wide view.
In Prizren there are mosques and churches from many centuries.
Every summer the film festival Dokufest takes place.

abschnitte.text: **Prizren** lies in the south of Kosovo, near the border with Albania and North Macedonia. Behind the city rise the mountains of the **Šar Mountains**. Even in the Middle Ages Prizren was an important trading town. Later it belonged for a long time to the **Ottoman Empire**, whose rulers sat in Istanbul. Many buildings of the old town date from that time.

abschnitte.titel: Bridge, fortress and places of worship
abschnitte.text: A small river, the Bistrica, flows through the middle of the old town. An old **stone bridge** from Ottoman times spans it. On the hill above the city stands the **fortress**, from which you look out over all the roofs. In the old town **mosques** and Orthodox and Catholic **churches** stand close together. The Sinan Pasha Mosque from the 17th century is well known.

In the lanes there are cafés, small shops and workshops where, for example, fine silver jewellery is made. Every summer the **Dokufest** takes place, a festival for documentary films. Then films are shown even in the open air and by the river. Many people from Kosovo who live in Switzerland also visit Prizren in summer.

gewusst: In Prizren mosques and churches often stand only a few steps from each other.
Prizren is known for filigree jewellery made of fine silver threads.

teile.einleitung: The Sagrada Família is a huge church in Barcelona in Spain. It was designed by the architect Antoni Gaudí and has been under construction since 1882. It is still not quite finished, yet it is one of the best-known buildings in the world.
wichtigste: The Sagrada Família is a church in Barcelona.
Its famous architect is Antoni Gaudí.
Building began in 1882.
The church is still not quite finished.
When it is complete, it will have 18 towers.
The tallest tower is dedicated to Jesus Christ.
The building work is paid for with donations and entrance fees.

abschnitte.text: The full name means roughly “Expiatory Temple of the Holy Family”. The **Sagrada Família** stands in **Barcelona**, the largest city in Catalonia. In **2010** Pope Benedict XVI consecrated it as a **basilica**, and services have been held there ever since. Millions of people visit the church every year. Parts of it are a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**.

Building began in **1882** to the plans of another architect. A year later the young **Antoni Gaudí** took over and redesigned everything. He worked on the church for more than 40 years, until his death in **1926**. Gaudí knew that he would not live to see it finished. He is said to have remarked that his client was in no hurry, meaning God.

Gaudí took great inspiration from **nature**. The **columns** inside branch out at the top like **trees**, and the roof looks like a canopy of leaves. Coloured light streams into the room through stained-glass windows. Outside there are three large **façades**: they tell of the birth of Jesus, of his suffering and of his glory. Everywhere you can see figures, plants and animals carved in stone.

When everything is finished, the church will have **18 towers**. Twelve stand for the **apostles**, four for the **evangelists** and one for **Mary**. The tallest, central tower is dedicated to **Jesus Christ**. With it, the Sagrada Família will become the tallest church in the world. Gaudí wanted it to stay a little lower than Montjuïc, the hill in Barcelona, because a work of humans should not be taller than a work of God.

The Sagrada Família receives no money from the state. The building work is paid for with **donations** and with the **entrance fees** of visitors. That is why progress was often slow in the past. Today computers and modern machines help to build the complicated stone shapes. People have been working on the church for more than 140 years.

gewusst: Antoni Gaudí is buried in the crypt of the Sagrada Família.
Gaudí worked on the church for more than 40 years and knew he would not live to see it finished.

teile.einleitung: Spain is a large country in the south-west of Europe. It lies on the Iberian Peninsula and is a parliamentary monarchy with a king. Besides Spanish, other languages are spoken in some regions.
wichtigste: Spain lies on the Iberian Peninsula, and the capital is Madrid.
The Pyrenees form the border with France.
Spain is a parliamentary monarchy.
The king is Felipe VI (as of 2026).
The country is divided into 17 autonomous communities.
In parts of Spain, Catalan, for example, is an official language.

abschnitte.text: Spain lies on the **Iberian Peninsula**, which it shares with Portugal. In the north the **Pyrenees** form the border with France. The small state of Andorra lies between them. Spain has coasts on the Mediterranean and the Atlantic. The country also includes the **Balearic Islands** in the Mediterranean and the **Canary Islands** in the Atlantic. In the interior lies a large plateau, on which the capital **Madrid** also stands.

Spain is a **parliamentary monarchy**. That means there is a king, but politics is made by the elected parliament and the government. The king is **Felipe VI** (as of 2026). He succeeded his father in 2014. The king represents the country, for example on state visits. Spain is a member of the EU, and people pay with the euro.

Spain is divided into **17 autonomous communities**, for example Andalusia, Catalonia or Galicia. Each has its own parliament and may decide many things itself. This is a little reminiscent of the cantons in Switzerland. Some regions would like even more independence. This is often discussed, and heatedly, in Spain.

Throughout the country people speak **Spanish**, also called Castilian. In some regions there are further official languages. In Catalonia, Valencia and the Balearic Islands it is **Catalan**. In Galicia people speak **Galician**, in the Basque Country **Basque**. Basque is special: it is not related to any other known language.

Spain has many famous buildings. In Granada stands the **Alhambra**, in Barcelona the **Sagrada Família** church by Antoni Gaudí. In the north Spanish city of **Bilbao** stands the **Guggenheim Museum**. Its curved façade of shining **titanium** looks like a huge ship made of metal. The museum has made the city known all over the world.

gewusst: The Sagrada Família in Barcelona has been under construction for more than 140 years.
The Canary Islands belong to Spain but lie off the coast of Africa.

teile.einleitung: Rügen is the largest island in Germany. It lies in the Baltic Sea and is famous for its white chalk cliffs, long sandy beaches and ancient beech forests. Many people spend their holidays there.
wichtigste: Rügen is the largest island in Germany.
The island lies in the Baltic Sea.
It belongs to the federal state of Mecklenburg-Vorpommern.
In Jasmund National Park there are white chalk cliffs.
The painter Caspar David Friedrich made the chalk cliffs famous.
Bridges connect Rügen with the city of Stralsund.
The small steam railway is called the “Rasender Roland”.

abschnitte.text: At almost 1000 square kilometres, **Rügen** is the **largest island in Germany**. It lies in the **Baltic Sea** and belongs to the federal state of **Mecklenburg-Vorpommern**. The coast is deeply indented, and many bays and peninsulas interlock. That is why the coastline is very long. At the far north lies **Cape Arkona** with its lighthouses.

In **Jasmund National Park** white **chalk cliffs** drop steeply into the sea. Chalk consists of the limy shells of tiny sea creatures that were deposited a very long time ago. The best-known cliff is called the **Königsstuhl**. Above the cliffs grow ancient **beech forests**, which are a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The painter **Caspar David Friedrich** painted the picture “Chalk Cliffs on Rügen” around 1818 and made the landscape famous.

Rügen is separated from the mainland by the **Strelasund**. Since 1936 the **Rügendamm** has led with road and railway to the city of **Stralsund**. Because there is a great deal of traffic in summer, the tall **Rügen Bridge** was also opened in 2007. Ships can pass beneath it. Ferries also connect the island with the mainland and with other countries.

Well-known **seaside resorts** such as Binz and Sellin have white villas and long piers. A special attraction is the **Rasender Roland**, a small **steam railway** on narrow-gauge track. Despite its name, the train travels leisurely slowly through the landscape. In spring and autumn many **cranes** rest on Rügen. The island is one of the most popular holiday regions in Germany.

gewusst: The white chalk of the cliffs consists of countless shells of tiny sea creatures.
The “Rasender Roland” (Racing Roland) has that name although it ambles rather gently across the island.

teile.einleitung: The Saimaa ringed seal is a small seal that lives only in Lake Saimaa in Finland. It is one of the rarest seals in the world. Because only a few hundred animals are left, it is strictly protected.
wichtigste: The Saimaa ringed seal lives only in Lake Saimaa in Finland.
It lives in fresh water, not in the sea.
Its ancestors were cut off in the lake after the last Ice Age.
Only a few hundred animals are left.
For its pups it needs snow on the ice.

abschnitte.text: The **Saimaa ringed seal** is a subspecies of the **ringed seal**, which otherwise lives in cold seas. It is found only in **Lake Saimaa** in Finland and lives in **fresh water**. Its ancestors were cut off in the lake after the **last Ice Age**, as the land slowly rose. Since then the animals have lived apart from their relatives in the sea. In Finnish the seal is called **Norppa**.

The seal eats mainly small **fish**. In winter, when the lake is frozen, it keeps **breathing holes** open in the ice. The females give birth to their pups in late winter in a **snow den** on the ice. There the little ones are protected from the cold and from enemies. In winters with little snow, helpers therefore pile up **heaps of snow** on the shore so that the seals can build dens.

The Saimaa ringed seal is **seriously endangered**, with only a few hundred animals left. In the past they were hunted, but today hunting is banned. A great danger is **fishing nets**, in which young seals can get tangled. That is why fishing bans apply in parts of the lake in spring. Thanks to these measures, the number of animals has slowly risen in recent years.

gewusst: In winters with little snow, people build artificial snow heaps so that the seals can make their dens.
The Saimaa ringed seal lives in fresh water, although its closest relatives live in the sea.

teile.einleitung: The Roma are a people who live in many countries of Europe. Their ancestors came about 1000 years ago from the north of India. With 10 to 12 million people they are the largest ethnic minority in Europe.
wichtigste: The ancestors of the Roma come from the north of India.
Their language Romani is related to Hindi.
An estimated 10 to 12 million Roma live in Europe.
International Roma Day is on 8 April.
The Roma flag shows a red wheel on blue and green.
In Switzerland the Yenish and Sinti have been recognised as a national minority since 2016.

abschnitte.text: For a long time people believed the Roma came from Egypt. That was wrong. **Comparisons of languages** and genetic studies show that their ancestors moved westwards about 1000 years ago from **northern India**. By way of Persia and the Byzantine Empire they came to Europe. Today Roma live in almost all countries of Europe, especially many in south-eastern Europe. Most have been settled for a long time.

The language of the Roma is called **Romani**. It belongs to the **Indo-Aryan languages** and is related to languages such as **Hindi**. On the way many words were added from Persian, Greek and other languages of Europe. Despite the similar name, Romani has nothing to do with the Romance languages such as Italian or Romansh. There are many different forms of the language.

On **8 April 1971** the first **World Romani Congress** took place in London. There a flag and an anthem were decided on. Since then 8 April has been **International Roma Day**. The flag is **blue** at the top for the sky and **green** at the bottom for the earth. In the middle stands a **red wheel**, which recalls the origin in India and life on the move.

Roma and Sinti were often disadvantaged and excluded in Europe. Under **National Socialism** they were persecuted, and hundreds of thousands were murdered. This genocide is often called **Porajmos** in Romani, roughly “the devouring”. In the night of 2 to 3 August 1944 the SS murdered the last roughly 4300 Sinti and Roma in a section of the camp at **Auschwitz-Birkenau**. That is why **2 August** has been the European day of remembrance for the victims since 2015.

In Switzerland too live Roma, Sinti and **Yenish**. The Yenish are a group of their own with their own language, who have lived in the country for a long time. In 2016 the Federal Council recognised the **Yenish and Sinti** as a **national minority**. This is meant to protect their culture and way of life, for example through stopping places for travellers. For a long time Yenish families in Switzerland were treated unjustly, for which the federal government has apologised.

gewusst: Romani is more closely related to Hindi than to any European language.
The red wheel on the Roma flag recalls the wheel on the flag of India.

teile.einleitung: Þingvellir is a national park in Iceland. There you can see how two great tectonic plates are drifting apart. It is also where the old parliament of the Icelanders once met.
wichtigste: Þingvellir lies in the south-west of Iceland, not far from Reykjavík.
Here the North American and the Eurasian plates meet.
You can hike in a rift between the plates.
From the year 930 the Althing, the assembly of the Icelanders, met here.
The park is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

abschnitte.text: The Earth’s crust consists of large **plates** that move very slowly. At Þingvellir the **North American** and the **Eurasian plates** are drifting apart, by a few millimetres every year. This creates long **rifts** and rock walls. You can hike on foot through such a gorge.

In the year 930 representatives from all over Iceland met here for the first time for the **Althing**. This assembly is regarded as one of the oldest parliaments in the world. People discussed laws and settled disputes. In 1944 the **Republic of Iceland** was proclaimed at Þingvellir.

In the park lies the largest natural lake in Iceland. In the rift called **Silfra** the water is so clear that you can see a long way. Divers swim there between the plates. Because of its nature and history, Þingvellir is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**.

gewusst: In the Silfra rift you can almost touch two tectonic plates at the same time with one hand.

teile.einleitung: Egypt lies in the north-east of Africa and is one of the best-known countries in the world. Here more than 5,000 years ago one of the first advanced civilisations arose, with pharaohs, pyramids and hieroglyphs. To this day the Nile is the lifeline of the country.
wichtigste: Egypt borders the Mediterranean in the north and the Red Sea in the east.
Most of the country is desert and belongs to the Sahara.
Almost all people live in the narrow Nile Valley and in the Nile Delta.
More than 100 million people live in Egypt (as of 2024).
The Suez Canal is one of the most important waterways in the world.
The Sinai Peninsula belongs geographically to Asia.
The capital is Cairo.

abschnitte.text: Egypt lies in the north-east of Africa. In the north it borders the **Mediterranean**, in the east the **Red Sea**, where there are colourful coral reefs. Most of the country is dry desert and belongs to the **Sahara**. East of the Suez Canal lies the **Sinai Peninsula**, which counts geographically as part of Asia. So Egypt lies on two continents.

The **Nile** flows from south to north through the whole country and runs into the Mediterranean in a large **delta**. Around 95 per cent of the people live on a narrow strip along the river. There the soil is fertile, and farmers can irrigate fields. The largest cities are the capital **Cairo** and the port city of **Alexandria**. More than 100 million people live in Egypt, more than ten times as many as in Switzerland.

The ancient Egyptians were ruled by kings called **pharaohs**. They built gigantic **pyramids** as tombs, for example at Giza near Cairo. Their writing consisted of picture signs, the **hieroglyphs**. Many animals were regarded as sacred, especially the **cat**. Numerous cat mummies have even been found.

The young pharaoh **Tutankhamun** became famous because his tomb was found almost untouched in 1922 in the **Valley of the Kings**. In it lay a magnificent **death mask of gold**. Much later, in 331 BC, **Alexander the Great** founded the city of Alexandria in the Nile Delta. It became famous for its great library and its lighthouse, which counted among the seven wonders of the ancient world.

The **Suez Canal** opened in 1869 and connects the Mediterranean with the Red Sea. Thanks to it, ships between Europe and Asia no longer have to sail all the way around Africa. That saves many days of travel time. For Egypt the canal is an important **source of income**, because the ships pay fees. **Tourism** to pyramids, temples and beaches is also very important for the country.

gewusst: Around 95 per cent of the people in Egypt live on only a small part of the country’s area, namely along the Nile.
The Great Pyramid of Giza is the only one of the seven wonders of the ancient world that still stands today.
The Lighthouse of Alexandria was also one of the seven wonders of the ancient world.

teile.einleitung: The Vardar is the longest river in North Macedonia. It flows through the capital Skopje and on into Greece, where it runs into the sea. In Greece it has a different name.
wichtigste: The Vardar is the longest river in North Macedonia.
It flows right through the capital Skopje.
In Greece the river is called the Axios.
It runs into the Aegean near Thessaloniki.
The Vardar valley is an important north-south route.

abschnitte.titel: From the mountains to the sea
abschnitte.text: The Vardar rises in the west of **North Macedonia** in the mountains. From there it flows east and then south right across the whole country. It is the **longest river** in North Macedonia. After the border it flows through Greece, where it is called the **Axios**. Near the city of **Thessaloniki** it runs into the **Aegean**, a part of the Mediterranean.

The Vardar flows through the middle of the capital **Skopje**. It divides the city into two halves. The old **Stone Bridge** joins the two banks and is a landmark of the city. On one side lies the old bazaar, on the other the modern centre.

The **Vardar valley** has been an important route through the Balkans for a very long time. It connects central Europe with the Mediterranean. Today a motorway and a railway line run there. A whole region is also named after the river, which used to be called **Vardar Macedonia**.

gewusst: A river can have two different names in two countries: Vardar in North Macedonia, Axios in Greece.

teile.einleitung: An agglomeration is a core city together with the surrounding municipalities that have grown together with it. Many people live in a suburban municipality and work in the city. In Switzerland a large part of the population lives in agglomerations.
wichtigste: An agglomeration consists of a core city and its suburbs.
The municipalities are closely tied to the core city.
Many people commute between their home and their workplace.
The largest agglomeration in Switzerland is that of Zurich.
The Federal Statistical Office decides which municipalities belong to it.

abschnitte.text: An **agglomeration** consists of a **core city** and the surrounding municipalities. These **suburbs** have grown together with the city. Often you can hardly tell where one municipality ends and the next begins. The **Zurich agglomeration**, for example, includes many municipalities around the city of Zurich.

In an agglomeration many people live in a suburb and work in the city, or the other way round. They **commute** every day by train, bus, bicycle or car. That is why good connections are important, for example an **S-Bahn**, a suburban rail network. The municipalities of an agglomeration often work together, for example on transport.

In Switzerland the **Federal Statistical Office** decides which municipalities belong to an agglomeration. Among other things it looks at how many people commute from a municipality into the core city. The largest agglomeration is that of **Zurich**. Other large agglomerations are Geneva, Basel, Bern and Lausanne. The Geneva and Basel agglomerations even extend across the national border.

gewusst: The Basel agglomeration extends as far as Germany and France.
In Switzerland the majority of the population lives in urban areas and their agglomerations.

teile.einleitung: Russia is the largest country in the world. It stretches from eastern Europe across the whole of northern Asia to the Pacific Ocean. Because it is so huge, it has icy tundra, endless forests, steppes and large cities.
wichtigste: Russia is the largest country in Europe and in the whole world.
Switzerland would fit into Russia more than 400 times.
The capital is Moscow, and the second largest city is Saint Petersburg.
The Trans-Siberian Railway runs from Moscow to the Pacific.
The flag has the colours white, blue and red.
Matryoshkas are colourful wooden dolls that nest inside each other.

abschnitte.text: At about **17 million square kilometres**, Russia is the **largest country in the world**. Switzerland would fit in **over 400 times**. The **Ural** mountains divide the country into a European and an Asian part. Most people live in the smaller European part. Because Russia is so wide, there are **eleven time zones** there: when it is evening in Moscow, it is already the next morning in the far east.

The **Trans-Siberian Railway** is one of the longest railway lines in the world. It runs from **Moscow** across Siberia to **Vladivostok** on the Pacific, which is over 9000 kilometres. A journey without stops takes about a week. On the way the train passes through dense forests called the **taiga** and past **Lake Baikal**. Lake Baikal is the deepest lake on Earth.

The capital **Moscow** is the largest city in the country. The **Kremlin** and Red Square with the colourful St Basil's Cathedral are well known there. The second largest city is **Saint Petersburg** on the Baltic Sea. Through the European part flows the **Volga**, the longest river in Europe. In Siberia there are much longer rivers that flow north into the Arctic Ocean.

The **flag** of Russia has three horizontal stripes in **white, blue and red**. A well-known souvenir is the **matryoshka**: painted wooden dolls with a smaller doll always inside. Russian writers such as Leo Tolstoy and composers such as Pyotr Tchaikovsky, who wrote the music for the ballet “Swan Lake”, are also famous. Russian is written with **Cyrillic letters**.

For a long time Russia was ruled by **tsars**. After the revolution of 1917 the **Soviet Union** arose, to which Russia belonged as the largest part. In 1991 the Soviet Union broke up, and Russia became a state of its own again. Since 2022 Russia has been waging war against Ukraine, which many countries, including Switzerland, have answered with sanctions.

gewusst: There are eleven different time zones in Russia.
Lake Baikal in Siberia is the deepest lake in the world and holds a great deal of fresh water.

teile.einleitung: The old-age dependency ratio shows how many older people there are for the people of working age. It is important for planning how pensions are financed. In Switzerland and in Europe it has been rising for years.
wichtigste: The old-age dependency ratio counts people aged 65 and over per 100 people aged 20 to 64.
The youth dependency ratio counts people under 20 per 100 people aged 20 to 64.
Both together make up the total dependency ratio.
Around 2023 the old-age dependency ratio in Switzerland was a little over 30.
A rising old-age dependency ratio is a challenge for the AHV, the state pension scheme.
Low birth rates and rising life expectancy make it rise.

abschnitte.text: The **Federal Statistical Office (FSO)** calculates it like this: you count the people aged **65 and over** and divide them by the people aged **20 to 64**. The result is given per 100 people. An old-age dependency ratio of **50** therefore means 50 older people for every 100 people of working age. For every two people able to work there is then one older person.

The **youth dependency ratio** counts the children and young people **under 20** per 100 people aged 20 to 64. If you add the youth and old-age dependency ratios together, you get the **total dependency ratio**. It shows how many young and old people there are for every 100 people of working age.

Around **2023** in Switzerland there were **a good 30 people aged 65 and over** for every 100 people between 20 and 64. The FSO expects a further marked rise in the coming decades. The reasons are **low birth rates** and **rising life expectancy**. When fewer children are born and people live longer, the older group grows compared with the working-age group.

abschnitte.titel: Why this matters for the AHV
abschnitte.text: The **AHV** works on a **pay-as-you-go basis**. That means the contributions of people in work directly pay for current pensions. If there are fewer people in work for each pensioner, financing becomes harder. That is why the old-age dependency ratio is an important topic in politics.

If you raise the age limit used in the calculation from 65 to **67 years**, the old-age dependency ratio **falls**. People aged 65 and 66 then count as part of the working-age group. In the short term, **immigration** of people of working age can also lower the ratio. Immigrants are often between 20 and 40 years old and so enlarge the working-age group.

gewusst: The old-age dependency ratio only says something about age, not about who actually works.
If you move the age limits used in the calculation, you change the old-age dependency ratio even though nobody has become older or younger.

teile.einleitung: Lake Balaton, in German Plattensee, is the largest lake in central Europe. It lies in Hungary and is a popular destination for beach holidays.
wichtigste: Lake Balaton lies in Hungary and is called Balaton in Hungarian.
It is about 77 kilometres long, but mostly only a few kilometres wide.
On average it is only about 3 metres deep.
It is jokingly called the “Hungarian Sea”.
On the Tihany peninsula stands an abbey that was founded in 1055.

abschnitte.text: **Lake Balaton** is the largest lake in central Europe. It is about **77 kilometres** long, but at most places only a few kilometres wide. What is special is that it is very **shallow**: on average it is only about **3 metres** deep. That is why the water warms up quickly in summer. In winter the lake often freezes over.

**Hungary** has no sea coast. That is why the big lake is jokingly called the **“Hungarian Sea”**. Many families take **beach holidays** there. On the shallow south shore, for example in **Siófok**, even small children can walk far out into the water. On the north shore there are hills where **wine** grows.

The **Tihany** peninsula reaches far into the lake. There stands an **abbey** that was founded in **1055**. Its foundation charter is famous because it contains some of the oldest known words in the **Hungarian language**. From Tihany you have a lovely view over the lake.

During the Cold War Europe was divided. Families from East and West Germany found it hard to visit each other. Many of them met on holiday at Lake Balaton in Hungary. In this way the lake became a special **meeting place**.

gewusst: Very close by lies the thermal lake of Hévíz, where you can swim even in winter.
Lake Balaton is somewhat larger than Lake Constance, but much less deep.

teile.einleitung: The Sierra Nevada is a high mountain range in the south of Spain. Its name means “snowy mountain range”. It lies in Andalusia right next to the city of Granada and has the highest mountains of the Iberian Peninsula.
wichtigste: The Sierra Nevada lies in Andalusia in the south of Spain.
The name means “snowy mountain range”.
The highest mountain is Mulhacén, and the second highest is Veleta.
The city of Granada lies at the foot of the mountains.
In 1996 the Alpine Ski World Championships took place here.
Since 1999 the Sierra Nevada has been a national park.

abschnitte.text: The Sierra Nevada lies in **Andalusia**, the southernmost region of Spain. Although it is very hot there in summer, snow often lies on the peaks for a long time. That is why the range is called the **“snowy mountain range”**. The Sierra Nevada belongs to the **Baetic System**, a larger mountain system in southern Spain. In clear weather you can see all the way to the Mediterranean from the top.

The highest mountain is **Mulhacén**, at almost 3,500 metres. It is the highest mountain on the Iberian Peninsula. It is named after a **Nasrid sultan of Granada**. The Nasrids were the last Muslim rulers in Spain. The second-highest peak is called **Veleta**. In the past a road even led almost to its top.

Right at the foot of the Sierra Nevada lies the city of **Granada**. There stands the famous **Alhambra**, built by the Nasrids. Behind the Alhambra you can often see the snow-covered peaks. The water from the mountains supplies the gardens and fields around the city.

In the Sierra Nevada there is one of the **southernmost ski areas in Europe**. In 1996 the **Alpine Ski World Championships** took place there. On the southern slope lie the **Alpujarras**, a landscape with white mountain villages and terraced fields. Since **1999** a large part of the range has been a **national park**, so that plants and animals are protected.

gewusst: In the Sierra Nevada you can ski in the morning and swim in the Mediterranean in the afternoon.
Plants grow in the Sierra Nevada that exist nowhere else in the world.

teile.einleitung: At around 6,961 metres, Aconcagua is the highest mountain in the Americas. It lies in the Andes in Argentina, near the border with Chile. No mountain outside Asia is higher.
wichtigste: Aconcagua is around 6,961 metres high.
It lies in the province of Mendoza in Argentina.
It is the highest peak of the Andes and of the Southern Hemisphere.
No mountain outside Asia is higher.
Matthias Zurbriggen, born in Saas-Fee, was the first to stand on the summit in 1897.
Thin air, cold and storms make the mountain dangerous.

abschnitte.titel: The highest mountain in the Americas
abschnitte.text: Aconcagua lies in the **province of Mendoza** in **Argentina**, near the border with Chile. It belongs to the **Andes**, which stretch for around 7,500 kilometres along the west coast of South America. At around **6,961 metres** it is their highest peak. It is the highest mountain of the **Southern Hemisphere** and of the **Western Hemisphere**, and the highest mountain outside Asia.

On **14 January 1897** the mountain guide **Matthias Zurbriggen** became the first person to stand on the summit. He was born in **Saas-Fee** in the Valais and grew up in **Macugnaga** in Piedmont. He was part of a **British expedition**. Zurbriggen later became known for many first ascents all over the world.

Aconcagua is **not regarded as an active volcano**. Very close by, on the border between Argentina and Chile, stands **Ojos del Salado**, though. It is around 6,893 metres high and lies on the edge of the **Atacama Desert**. It is regarded as the **highest volcano on Earth** and, after Aconcagua, the second-highest mountain in South America.

The **normal route** up Aconcagua is not technically difficult, so you do not need to climb. Even so, the mountain is dangerous. At almost 7,000 metres the air is very **low in oxygen**. Storms bring great **cold**. Many mountaineers underestimate **altitude sickness**.

gewusst: Aconcagua is more than 2,300 metres higher than the Dufourspitze, the highest peak in Switzerland.
The first climber, Matthias Zurbriggen, came from Saas-Fee in the Valais.

teile.einleitung: Auroras, also called polar lights, are glowing bands and curtains in the night sky that shimmer green, red or violet. They arise when particles from the Sun hit the Earth's atmosphere. They are seen most often in the far north and the far south.
wichtigste: Auroras arise from particles from the Sun that hit the atmosphere.
The common green light comes from excited oxygen.
Red aurora forms at very great height, where the air is very thin.
Auroras are most frequent in the auroral oval around the magnetic poles.
The Kp index from 0 to 9 shows how strongly the Earth's magnetic field is disturbed.
In May 2024 auroras could even be seen well in Switzerland.

abschnitte.text: The Sun constantly hurls electrically charged particles into space. This stream is called the **solar wind**. The **magnetic field** of the Earth deflects most of the particles, but guides some towards the poles. There, at great height, they collide with particles of the air and give them energy. The air particles are said to be **excited**. When they release the energy again, they glow.

abschnitte.titel: Why it glows green and red
abschnitte.text: The colour depends on which gas glows and at what height. The most common **green** comes from excited **oxygen atoms**, which emit light with a wavelength of 557.7 nanometres. **Red** light is given off by oxygen only at very great height. For that an atom has to stay excited for a long time without colliding with other particles, and this works only in very thin air. Violet and bluish tones come mainly from nitrogen.

Auroras are most frequent in a ring-shaped area around the magnetic poles, the **auroral oval**. It lies roughly between 65 and 75 degrees of magnetic latitude, that is, over northern Norway, northern Sweden, Finland, Iceland, Canada and Alaska. A well-known place is **Abisko** in Swedish Lapland. It lies in the rain shadow of the mountains, so the sky there is often clear. When solar activity is strong, the oval extends southwards.

The activity of the Sun varies in a **sunspot cycle** of about 11 years. Around the maximum there are more solar storms and therefore more auroras. Forecasts use the **Kp index**, which runs from 0 to 9. The higher the value, the further south auroras can be seen. On 10 and 11 May 2024 a very strong storm hit the Earth, and auroras could be seen as far as southern and central Europe, including Switzerland.

In 1859 the English astronomer **Richard Carrington** observed a strong eruption on the Sun. The storm that followed is today called the **Carrington Event**. It disrupted telegraph lines, and auroras were visible as far as the tropics. A storm that strong could today disrupt satellites and power grids.

gewusst: In Finnish auroras are called “revontulet”, which means “fox fires”. According to a legend, an Arctic fox whisks up snow with its tail, and it sparkles in the sky.
Auroras also occur on other planets with a magnetic field, for example on Jupiter and Saturn.

teile.einleitung: The Tagus is the longest river on the Iberian Peninsula. It rises in Spain, flows west through Portugal and runs into the Atlantic at Lisbon. Famous cities and buildings lie on its banks.
wichtigste: The Tagus rises in the mountains in the east of Spain.
In Spanish it is called Tajo and in Portuguese Tejo.
It runs into the Atlantic Ocean at Lisbon.
The old city of Toledo is almost completely surrounded by the Tagus.
In Lisbon the “25 de Abril” Bridge and the Vasco da Gama Bridge cross the river.
The Belém Tower stands on the bank.

abschnitte.text: The **Tagus** is about 1,000 kilometres long and so the longest river on the Iberian Peninsula. It begins in the mountains in the east of **Spain** and flows west. For a stretch it forms the border between Spain and Portugal. In Spain it is called the **Tajo**, and in Portugal the **Tejo**. But it is the same river.

In Spain the Tagus flows in a great loop almost all the way round the old town of **Toledo**. The city lies on a hill and was well protected as a result. In the region of Extremadura stands the **Roman bridge of Alcántara**. It was built around AD 104 to 106 under Emperor Trajan and still stands today. The place name comes from Arabic and means “the bridge”.

At **Lisbon**, the capital of Portugal, the river becomes very wide and runs into the **Atlantic**. On the bank stands the **Belém Tower**, which was built about 500 years ago. It was meant to protect the entrance to the harbour. From here Portuguese seafarers once set off on their great voyages of discovery.

The red suspension bridge **Ponte 25 de Abril** was opened in 1966. It hangs from large cables and looks very similar to the **Golden Gate Bridge** in San Francisco. It has borne its name since the revolution of 25 April 1974. Further upstream lies the **Vasco da Gama Bridge**. It opened in 1998, is more than 17 kilometres long and is named after the famous seafarer.

gewusst: The Vasco da Gama Bridge is among the longest bridges in Europe.
The Roman bridge of Alcántara is almost 2,000 years old and is still in use.

teile.einleitung: Neuschwanstein Castle is a famous castle in Bavaria in the south of Germany. King Ludwig II had it built in the 19th century as if out of a fairy tale. Today more than a million people visit it every year.
wichtigste: King Ludwig II of Bavaria had Neuschwanstein built.
The castle stands in Germany on the edge of the Alps.
Because of its looks, it is often called a fairy-tale castle.
The wall paintings show stories from operas by Richard Wagner.
The castle was never completely finished.
The king lived in it for only a few months.
The most famous view is from the Marienbrücke.

abschnitte.text: **Neuschwanstein** stands on a rock above a gorge near Füssen in the **Allgäu**, right on the edge of the **Alps**. With its white walls and many turrets, it looks like something from a picture book. That is why it is often called a **fairy-tale castle**. The foundation stone was laid in 1869. Very close by stands the yellow Hohenschwangau Castle, where Ludwig spent a lot of time as a child.

The builder was King **Ludwig II** of Bavaria. He loved legends, knights and music and built himself a world out of his dreams. Besides Neuschwanstein he also had the castles of Linderhof and Herrenchiemsee built. He spent a great deal of money on them and ran up large debts. In **1886** he was declared unfit to rule and died soon afterwards in Lake Starnberg.

Ludwig II admired the composer **Richard Wagner**. The **wall paintings** in the castle show stories from Wagner’s operas, for example about the swan knight **Lohengrin** and the singer Tannhäuser. That is why you find many **swans** in the castle. The magnificent **Singers’ Hall** recalls a medieval castle. At the same time the castle had modern technology, such as warm-air heating and running water.

The castle was **never completely finished**. When Ludwig died in 1886, many rooms were still empty. He himself lived in it for **only a few months**. Soon after his death the castle was opened to visitors. Since 2025 it has been a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**, together with the king’s other castles.

The most famous view of Neuschwanstein is from the **Marienbrücke**. It leads high over the **Pöllat Gorge** with a waterfall. From there you can see the castle in front of the mountains and the Alpine foothills. Neuschwanstein served as a model for the Sleeping Beauty castle in the Disney theme parks. It is one of the most visited castles in Europe.

gewusst: King Ludwig II lived in his dream castle for only a few months.
Neuschwanstein was a model for the castle in the Disney parks.

teile.einleitung: Agribusiness covers all the branches of the economy that have to do with our food. These include seeds, fertiliser and machinery, farming itself, and the processing and trading of food. Very large corporations are often involved.
wichtigste: Agribusiness covers the whole chain from seeds to trade.
The term “agribusiness” was coined in 1957 at Harvard Business School.
The Basel agricultural group Syngenta was taken over by ChemChina in 2017.
In 2018 Bayer took over the seed company Monsanto.
The four largest grain traders are called “ABCD”.
Geneva is an important trading hub for agricultural commodities.

abschnitte.text: **Agribusiness** covers the whole **value chain** of food. It begins with **seeds**, **fertiliser** and **machinery**. Then comes **farming** in the field and in the stable. After that come the **food industry** and **trade**. The term “agribusiness” was coined by **John Davis** and **Ray Goldberg** of **Harvard Business School** in 1957.

In agribusiness there are a few very large companies. The agrochemicals and seed company **Syngenta**, based in **Basel**, was taken over in 2017 by the Chinese state-owned company **ChemChina**, for around 43 billion US dollars. Its headquarters stayed in Basel. In 2018 the German company **Bayer** bought the US company **Monsanto** for around 63 billion US dollars.

A large part of the world’s trade in **grain** and **oilseeds** is handled by a few corporations. They are called **ABCD** after their initial letters: **ADM**, **Bunge**, **Cargill** and **Louis Dreyfus**. Switzerland plays an important part in this. In the **Geneva** region many large commodity traders have their headquarters or important branches.

Many corporations control **several stages** of the chain at once. This is called **vertical integration**. A corporation then owns, for example, feed mills, fattening farms, slaughterhouses and distribution all at the same time. In this way it can control costs and quality better.

In **contract farming**, farmers deliver to a buyer on terms agreed in advance. Quantity, quality and often the price are fixed before sowing. Farmers have more security this way, but also become **dependent**. Many also buy **hybrid seed**. It is produced by crossing two parent lines and is especially high-yielding in the first generation. Because the next generation loses these advantages, farmers have to buy it again every year.

gewusst: At the time, the takeover of Syngenta was the largest takeover by a Chinese company.
Although Switzerland grows little grain, a large part of the world trade in agricultural commodities is handled from Geneva.

teile.einleitung: Sardinia is a large island in the Mediterranean and belongs to Italy. It is known for its turquoise sea, ancient stone towers and many sheep. After Sicily, it is the second-largest island in the Mediterranean.
wichtigste: Sardinia belongs to Italy.
It is the second-largest island in the Mediterranean.
The capital is called Cagliari.
The ancient stone towers are called nuraghes.
There are more sheep than people on the island.
North of Sardinia lies the French island of Corsica.
Flamingos live in the lagoons.

abschnitte.text: **Sardinia** lies in the Mediterranean **west** of the Italian mainland. After **Sicily** it is the **second-largest island in the Mediterranean**. Directly to the north lies the French island of **Corsica**, separated by a narrow strait. Sardinia is an **autonomous region** of Italy and manages some matters itself. The capital is **Cagliari** in the south.

On Sardinia there are thousands of **nuraghes**. These are round **stone towers** that were built more than 3,000 years ago from large stones without mortar. What exactly they were used for is not quite certain: perhaps as dwelling towers, fortresses or meeting places. The large complex of **Su Nuraxi** near Barumini is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**. A whole culture is also named after the nuraghes, the **Nuragic culture**.

On Sardinia there are **more sheep than people**.
