Sheep farming has a long tradition, especially in the mountainous interior of the island. **Pecorino**, a spicy cheese, is made from the sheep’s milk. A typical bread is the wafer-thin, crispy **carasau**. Besides Italian, many people on Sardinia speak **Sardinian**, a Romance language of its own.

Sardinia has many beaches with pale sand and clear, **turquoise** water. In the north-east lies the famous **Costa Smeralda**, the Emerald Coast, with exclusive holiday resorts. In the **lagoons**, for example near Cagliari, you can watch **flamingos**. Inland there are mountains, gorges and cork oak forests. Many visitors from Switzerland spend their summer holidays here.

gewusst: The nuraghes were built without mortar, and some have stood for more than 3,000 years.
On Sardinia, an unusually large number of people live to be over 100.

teile.einleitung: After Lisbon, Porto is the second largest city in Portugal. It lies in the north of the country where the River Douro flows into the Atlantic. Porto is famous for its colourful old town, its bridges and port wine.
wichtigste: Porto is the second largest city in Portugal.
The city lies on the River Douro, just before the Atlantic.
The Dom Luís I Bridge has two levels.
Opposite, in Vila Nova de Gaia, many port wine cellars store their wine.
The name Portugal goes back to “Portus Cale”, the old name of the area.
The old town district of Ribeira is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

abschnitte.text: **Porto** lies on steep slopes above the River **Douro**, a few kilometres before it flows into the **Atlantic**. The city is the economic centre of northern Portugal. In English its name simply means “the port”. The Romans already called the settlement at the mouth of the Douro **Portus Cale**. From this name the name of the whole country later arose: **Portugal**.

Several large bridges cross the Douro. The best known is the **Dom Luís I Bridge**, an iron arch bridge that opened in 1886. It has two levels: on the top the **metro** runs, and below cars drive. On foot you can cross the river on both levels and have a wide view of the city.

On the bank of the Douro lies the old district of **Ribeira** with narrow lanes and colourful houses. Many facades are decorated with blue and white tiles, the **azulejos**. Since 1996 the old town of Porto has been a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**. Above the city rises the tower of the church of **Torre dos Clérigos**, a landmark of Porto.

On the south bank lies the town of **Vila Nova de Gaia**. There **port wine**, a sweet, strong wine, matures in large cellars. The grapes for it grow further up in the Douro valley on steep terraces. In the past flat wooden boats, the **rabelos**, carried the barrels down the river. Today a few of these boats lie in front of the cellars as a reminder.

In Porto **Henry the Navigator** was born in 1394. He promoted the voyages of discovery of the Portuguese along the coast of Africa. Today the city is also known for the football club **FC Porto**. A typical speciality is the **francesinha**, a thick, warm sandwich with sauce.

gewusst: The name of the country Portugal comes from the area around Porto.
On the upper level of the Dom Luís I Bridge a metro crosses the Douro.

teile.einleitung: Denmark is a pioneering country for wind energy. More than a hundred years ago electricity was already being generated there with wind turbines, and the world’s first offshore wind farm went into operation off its coast. Today the country covers more than half of its electricity needs with wind.
wichtigste: In 2023 Denmark covered more than half of its electricity needs with wind energy.
Vindeby went into operation in 1991 as the world’s first offshore wind farm.
From 1891 Poul la Cour researched wind turbines for generating electricity in Askov.
Vestas from Aarhus is one of the largest makers of wind turbines.
Ørsted, formerly DONG Energy, is one of the largest offshore operators in the world.
The “Danish concept” means three rotor blades on the windward side.

abschnitte.text: From **1891** **Poul la Cour** carried out scientific experiments with wind turbines in **Askov**. He generated electricity with them and stored the energy as **hydrogen**. He is regarded as the **father of Danish wind energy**. In 1957 **Johannes Juul** built the **Gedser turbine**. It had three blades that run facing the wind in front of the tower, that is, on the **windward side**. Almost all of today’s large turbines use this **Danish concept**.

Wind turbines at sea are called **offshore installations**. The world’s first offshore wind farm was **Vindeby**, off the island of Lolland. It went into operation in **1991** with eleven turbines, ran for 25 years and was dismantled in 2017. In 2002 came **Horns Rev 1** in the North Sea west of Esbjerg. With 80 turbines and 160 megawatts, it is regarded as the world’s first **large** offshore wind farm.

The Danish manufacturer **Vestas**, headquartered in **Aarhus**, is one of the largest producers of wind turbines in the world. The energy group **DONG Energy** sold its oil and gas business and in 2017 renamed itself **Ørsted**. The name honours the Danish physicist **Hans Christian Ørsted**. Today Ørsted is one of the largest operators of offshore wind farms.

Off **Copenhagen** stands the **Middelgrunden** wind farm with 20 turbines. It went into operation in 2000. Half of the turbines belong to a **cooperative** with thousands of members from the public. This kind of **citizen participation** has helped to make many people in Denmark support wind power.

In **2023** Denmark covered **more than half** of its electricity needs with wind energy. That is one of the highest shares in the world. Denmark is planning **energy islands** in the North Sea and the Baltic Sea, among others near **Bornholm**. There, the electricity from many wind farms is to be collected and sent, for example, to Germany. In Switzerland, by contrast, wind energy has so far played only a small part.

gewusst: As early as the 19th century, Poul la Cour was storing wind power as hydrogen.
The world’s first offshore wind farm, Vindeby, ran for 25 years.

teile.einleitung: Tyrol is a federal state in the west of Austria. It is shaped by high mountains and borders Switzerland, Germany and Italy. The capital is Innsbruck.
wichtigste: Tyrol is one of the nine federal states of Austria.
The capital is called Innsbruck.
Tyrol borders Switzerland, Germany and, in the south, Italy.
The highest mountain is the Wildspitze at about 3,770 metres.
In Kitzbühel the Hahnenkamm race takes place on the Streif.
The coat of arms shows a red eagle on a white background.

abschnitte.text: **Tyrol** is one of the nine **federal states** of Austria. It borders the canton of the Grisons in Switzerland, Germany and Italy. Almost the whole land lies in the Alps. The highest mountain is the **Wildspitze** in the Ötztal Alps, which is about 3,770 metres high. The **Inn**, which rises in the Engadine in Switzerland, flows through the main valley.

The capital **Innsbruck** lies in the Inn valley between high mountains. In the old town stands the **Golden Roof** (Goldenes Dachl). It is an oriel window whose roof is covered with gilded copper tiles. It was built more than 500 years ago for Emperor Maximilian I. Innsbruck hosted the Winter Olympic Games twice, in 1964 and 1976.

Tyrol is a popular destination for ski holidays. Especially famous is the **Streif** in **Kitzbühel**. The **Hahnenkamm race** takes place on this piste every year, one of the most difficult downhill runs in the world. Swiss skiers have also won here. In summer many people come for hiking and mountaineering.

abschnitte.titel: Coat of arms, history and dumplings
abschnitte.text: The **coat of arms** of Tyrol shows a red eagle on a white background. In the past Tyrol was larger. After the First World War the southern part went to Italy and is now called **South Tyrol**. **Dumplings** (Knödel) are part of Tyrolean cooking. They are made from stale bread, often with bacon, and eaten in soup or with sauerkraut.

gewusst: The Golden Roof is covered with more than 2,000 gilded copper tiles.
The Inn, which flows through Innsbruck, comes from Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: Tuscany is a region in central Italy. It is known for gentle hills with cypress trees, for wine and for famous cities such as Florence, Pisa and Siena. Many artists and poets come from here.
wichtigste: The capital of Tuscany is Florence.
The famous leaning tower stands in Pisa.
Slender cypresses shape the landscape.
The Palio horse race takes place in Siena.
Napoleon was exiled to the island of Elba in 1814.
The name Tuscany goes back to the Etruscan people.

abschnitte.text: **Tuscany** lies in central Italy by the sea. Typical are gentle hills, vineyards, olive trees and tall, slender **cypresses** lining roads and farms. Between Florence and Siena lies the wine region of **Chianti**, which is known for its red wine. Off the coast lies the island of **Elba**. Napoleon was exiled there in 1814, but in 1815 he escaped back to France.

The capital of the region is **Florence**, a centre of art with many museums and churches. In **Pisa** stands the famous **leaning tower**, the bell tower of the cathedral. It already leaned while it was being built, because the ground beneath it is soft. In **Siena** the **Palio** takes place twice in summer. In this horse race the city districts compete against each other on the Piazza del Campo.

The name Tuscany goes back to the **Etruscans**, a people who lived here before the Romans. The Romans called their region “Tuscia”, which became Toscana. In the 14th century the poets **Dante, Petrarch and Boccaccio** wrote in the everyday language of Florence. As a result, Florentine became a respected language. After the unification of Italy it became established as the basis of **standard Italian**.

The town of **Carrara** is world famous for its white **marble**. It has been quarried in the mountains above it since Roman times, and Michelangelo also chose blocks of stone here. In **Larderello** hot steam comes out of the ground. In 1904 electricity was generated there from **geothermal energy** for the first time, and light bulbs were lit with it. Later the world’s first geothermal power plant was built in this place.

gewusst: Because Dante wrote in the language of Florence, all of Italy, and Ticino too, speak an Italian today that is based on Tuscan.
The Leaning Tower of Pisa was already leaning before it was finished.

teile.einleitung: A ria coast is a coast with bays reaching deep inland. These bays, the rias, are former river valleys into which the sea has penetrated. The best-known example is the coast of Galicia in the north-west of Spain.
wichtigste: A ria is a river valley flooded by the sea.
Rias formed when the sea level rose after the last ice age.
Unlike fjords, rias were never scoured out by glaciers.
The word “ria” comes from Galician.
Many mussels are farmed in the Rías Baixas.
The largest Galician ria is the Ría de Arousa.

abschnitte.text: During the last **ice age** a lot of water was locked up in huge ice sheets, and the sea level lay low. When the ice melted, the sea level rose worldwide by over 100 metres. The sea thereby penetrated far into the **lower courses** of rivers. In this way the river valleys became long, often branching bays. These bays are called **rias**, and the coast a **ria coast**.

Rias and **fjords** look alike at first glance. But they formed differently. A ria is a **river valley** with a V-shaped cross section that was flooded only by the rising sea level. A fjord, by contrast, is a valley that a **glacier** scoured out deeply, with a U-shaped cross section. Rias are counted among the **transverse coasts**, because the valleys reach inland roughly at right angles to the coastline. Between the bays lie peninsulas.

The word **“ría”** comes from Galician and is related to **“río”**, river. From the coast of **Galicia** in the north-west of Spain the term was taken over into geography. A distinction is made between the **Rías Altas** in the north, for example near A Coruña and Ferrol, and the **Rías Baixas** in the south. “Baixas” means “lower”. They include the **Ría de Vigo**, and the largest is the **Ría de Arousa**.

The Rías Baixas have calm, nutrient-rich water. There **mussels** hang on ropes under floating wooden rafts, the **“bateas”**. Galicia is among the largest mussel producers in the world. Off the Ría de Vigo lie the **Illas Cíes**. They protect the bay like a natural breakwater and since 2002 have been part of the Atlantic Islands of Galicia National Park.

Ria coasts also occur in other regions with river valleys on the sea. Examples are **Brittany** in France, the south-west of England and the south-west of **Ireland**. Switzerland has no sea coast, but here too the end of the ice age greatly shaped the landscape, for example through the many lakes.

gewusst: The mussel rafts in the rias are called “bateas” and carry ropes on which the mussels grow.
In the last ice age the sea level lay over 100 metres lower than today.

teile.einleitung: Rijeka is a port city in the north of Croatia on the Adriatic. It has the largest port in the country. The city lies in the Kvarner Bay between the Istrian peninsula and the mountains.
wichtigste: Rijeka lies in the Kvarner Bay in the north of the Adriatic.
Rijeka has the largest cargo port in Croatia.
The name Rijeka means “river”.
In 2020 Rijeka was a European Capital of Culture.
The carnival of Rijeka is the largest in Croatia.

abschnitte.text: **Rijeka** lies on the **Kvarner Bay** in the north of the Adriatic. The port is the largest and most important **cargo port** in Croatia. Here goods are loaded onto ships and carried on by rail and lorry into the interior, as far as Hungary and central Europe. For a long time Rijeka also had large shipyards where ships were built.

Through the city flows the small river **Rječina**. The name **Rijeka** means “river” in Croatian. The Italian name **Fiume** also means “river”. In the course of history the city belonged to different states, such as Austria-Hungary and Italy. In Rijeka the **torpedo**, a weapon for ships, was developed in the 19th century. Above the city stands the old castle of **Trsat**.

In **2020** Rijeka was a **European Capital of Culture** together with Galway in Ireland. Every year the city celebrates a large **carnival** with parades and masks. It is the largest carnival in Croatia. Like the Fasnacht in Basel or Lucerne, it attracts many visitors.

gewusst: Both the Croatian name Rijeka and the Italian name Fiume mean “river”.
Rijeka was a European Capital of Culture in 2020.

teile.einleitung: Sápmi is the homeland of the Sami in the far north of Europe. The Sami call it that in their own language. The region stretches across four states and is often known in English as Lapland.
wichtigste: Sápmi is the Sami name for the Sami homeland.
It is spread across four states: Norway, Sweden, Finland and Russia.
The Russian Kola Peninsula is also part of Sápmi.
In English people often speak of Lapland.
Many Sami traditionally keep reindeer.
In Norway, Sweden and Finland the Sami have their own parliaments.

abschnitte.text: **Sápmi** lies in the north of Norway, Sweden and Finland and reaches as far as the Russian **Kola Peninsula**. There are wide forests, bogs, mountains and long, cold winters there. In summer, north of the Arctic Circle, the sun does not set for weeks. The area has no state borders of its own. It is the home of a people who live in four states.

The **Sami** are an **indigenous people**, that is, a people who lived in this area for a very long time before today’s states came into being. In the past they were called Lapps, but many Sami find this word foreign and insulting. Traditionally many lived from **reindeer herding**, fishing and hunting. Today most Sami work in quite ordinary jobs, but reindeer herding is still important for their culture.

There are several **Sami languages**, which are related to Finnish. A special form of singing is the **joik**, with which people describe a person, an animal or a landscape. The Sami have their own flag and a national day on 6 February. In Norway, Sweden and Finland there are Sami parliaments that stand up for language and culture. In the past Sami culture was often suppressed in these countries, but today it is better protected.

gewusst: With a joik you do not sing about someone, you “joik” the person or the landscape itself.
Sápmi is bigger than many European countries, but has no state border of its own.

teile.einleitung: The United Kingdom is a state in the north-west of Europe. It consists of four countries and is headed by a king or queen as head of state. The capital is London.
wichtigste: The United Kingdom consists of England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.
Great Britain is only the large island, and Northern Ireland also belongs to the kingdom.
The flag is called the Union Jack.
The country is a parliamentary monarchy, and since 2022 Charles III has been king.
In mid-2024 about 69 million people lived there.
The capital is London.

abschnitte.text: The United Kingdom includes **England**, **Scotland**, **Wales** and **Northern Ireland**. The first three lie on the large island of **Great Britain**. Northern Ireland lies in the north-east of the island of **Ireland**. The Republic of Ireland in the south is a separate state. That is why “United Kingdom” is the more exact name than “Great Britain”.

The flag is called the **Union Jack** or Union Flag. It combines the crosses of three patron saints. The red **St George’s Cross** stands for England. The white diagonal **St Andrew’s Cross** on a blue background stands for Scotland and forms the background. The red diagonal **St Patrick’s Cross** stands for Ireland. Wales is not represented in the flag.

The country is a **parliamentary monarchy**. The head of state is a king or queen, and since 2022 it has been **Charles III**. The country is governed, though, by **Parliament** in London and by the **Prime Minister**. Parliament has two chambers: the House of Commons and the House of Lords. Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland also have parliaments of their own for some matters.

In mid-2024 about **69 million people** lived in the United Kingdom. That is almost eight times as many as in Switzerland. The largest city is **London**, an important place for banking and trade. People pay with the **pound sterling**. In 2016 the population voted to leave the European Union, the so-called **Brexit**, which took effect in 2020.

gewusst: In the 18th century the Industrial Revolution began in Great Britain with the first large factories.
“Big Ben” is actually the name of the large bell in the clock tower of Parliament in London.

teile.einleitung: Petrovaradin, in German Peterwardein, is a large fortress in the city of Novi Sad in Serbia. It stands high above the bank of the Danube and is now a popular place for culture and music.
wichtigste: The Petrovaradin Fortress lies in Novi Sad on the bank of the Danube.
In the 18th century it was extended by Austria.
In 1716 Prince Eugene won a battle here against the Ottomans.
On the clock tower the hands are swapped.
Every year a large music festival takes place here.

abschnitte.text: The **Petrovaradin** fortress stands on a rock on the right bank of the **Danube**, opposite the old town of **Novi Sad**. The region long belonged to the realm of the **Habsburgs**. In the **18th century** the Austrians greatly extended the fortress to protect themselves against the **Ottoman Empire**. Beneath the fortress there are long underground passages.

In **1716** a great **battle** took place at Petrovaradin between the army of the Habsburgs and the Ottomans. The Habsburgs under **Prince Eugene** of Savoy won. After that the Ottomans withdrew further from the region.

The **clock tower** of the fortress is well known. On its clock the **hands are swapped**: the big hand shows the hours and the small one the minutes. This way boatmen on the Danube could read the hour even from far away. Every summer the great music festival **EXIT** takes place at the fortress. In 2022 Novi Sad was a **European Capital of Culture**.

gewusst: Because of the swapped hands, the clock tower is also called the “drunken clock”.

teile.einleitung: Wine has been grown in Europe for thousands of years. Many regions are world famous for their wines, and some vineyards even belong to the World Heritage. Switzerland also has well-known wine-growing areas, especially in the Valais and on Lake Geneva.
wichtigste: Only sparkling wine from Champagne may be called champagne.
The Rioja in Spain is known for red wines made from Tempranillo.
Port comes from the Douro Valley in Portugal.
Lavaux on Lake Geneva has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2007.
The Valais has the largest vineyard area in Switzerland.
Chasselas is the most important white grape variety in western Switzerland.
Riesling is mainly grown on the Moselle.

abschnitte.text: Wine is made from **grapes** that grow on **vines**. Vines like sun and slopes where water drains away well. The grapes are harvested in autumn. In Switzerland this harvest is often called the **Wümmet**. The grapes are pressed into juice, which is fermented into wine. Wine contains alcohol and is only for adults, but the same grapes also give **grape juice**.

France is one of the biggest wine countries in the world. Only sparkling wine from the **Champagne** region in the north-east may be called **champagne**, as the name is protected. In Germany the area on the **Moselle** is well known. On the steep **slate slopes** there it is mainly **Riesling**, a white grape variety, that grows.

The **Rioja** lies in the north of **Spain** on the River Ebro. It is known for red wines made from the **Tempranillo** grape. In the **Douro Valley** in **Portugal** **port** is made. It gets its name from the city of **Porto**, from where it was shipped. In the north-east of **Hungary** lies the area of **Tokaj**, famous for its sweet wines.

The largest vineyard area in Switzerland belongs to the canton of **Valais**, around a third of the whole area. The sunny, dry climate is ideal for it. The most important white grape variety in western Switzerland is **Chasselas**. In the Valais the wine made from it is called **Fendant**. Between Lausanne and Montreux lie the vine terraces of **Lavaux**. They were built up over centuries on the steep slopes and have been part of the **UNESCO World Heritage** since **2007**.

gewusst: The vine terraces in Lavaux are held up by thousands of stone walls.
Even the ancient Romans planted vines in many parts of Europe.

teile.einleitung: The Great Belt Fixed Link is a permanent crossing over the Great Belt in Denmark. It connects the islands of Zealand and Funen with bridges and a railway tunnel. In the past you had to cross there by ferry.
wichtigste: The link crosses the Great Belt, a strait between Zealand and Funen.
It consists of two large bridges and a railway tunnel.
In the middle lies the small island of Sprogø.
Trains have crossed without a ferry since 1997, and cars since 1998.
You pay a toll to cross by car.

abschnitte.text: The **Great Belt** is a wide strait between the Danish islands of Zealand and Funen. The link across it is almost 18 kilometres long in total. Between Funen and the small island of **Sprogø** a long bridge carries road and rail. From Sprogø to Zealand, cars drive over a large **suspension bridge**, while trains go through a tunnel under the sea floor. The suspension bridge is among the longest of its kind in Europe.

Before the link was built, cars and trains had to cross the Great Belt by **ferry**. It took a long time, and in storms crossings were cancelled. Since 1997 trains have gone through the tunnel, and since 1998 cars have driven over the bridges. Today the crossing takes only a few minutes. The link is important because it connects the capital Copenhagen on Zealand with the west of Denmark.

abschnitte.titel: Plenty of traffic on the water
abschnitte.text: The Great Belt is also an important waterway between the **Baltic Sea** and the North Sea. That is why the suspension bridge had to be built very high, so that large ships can pass underneath. Its towers rise far above the sea. For using the bridge, drivers pay a toll, which is used to pay the high building costs.

gewusst: The island of Sprogø in the middle of the link was artificially enlarged for the construction.
Anyone travelling by train from Copenhagen to the west today often hardly notices that they are going under the sea.

teile.einleitung: Lake Prespa lies in the south-west of the Balkans. At it the borders of three countries meet: North Macedonia, Albania and Greece. It lies high in the mountains and is an important habitat for birds.
wichtigste: At Great Prespa Lake, North Macedonia, Albania and Greece meet.
It lies higher than the neighbouring Lake Ohrid.
Its water flows underground through the rock into Lake Ohrid.
Besides the large one there is Small Prespa Lake.
Rare birds such as pelicans live at the lake.

abschnitte.text: There are two Prespa lakes: **Great Prespa Lake** and **Small Prespa Lake**. Great Prespa Lake is shared by **North Macedonia**, **Albania** and **Greece**. In the middle of the lake the three borders meet. Small Prespa Lake lies largely in Greece. Both lakes lie in a basin between high mountains.

Lake Prespa lies higher than the neighbouring **Lake Ohrid**, by about 150 metres. Between the two lakes lies a mountain range of **limestone**. In this rock there are fissures and caves through which water can flow. In this way water from Lake Prespa reaches Lake Ohrid **underground** and feeds it. Such landscapes with caves and underground rivers are called **karst**.

Around the lakes there are reeds, marshes and forests. Many waterbirds live here, including rare **pelicans**. Large parts of the area are protected, and in all three countries there are protected areas and national parks. The three states work together to protect the lakes.

gewusst: Lake Prespa is one of the few lakes where three countries meet.
Water from Lake Prespa, after its journey through the mountain, comes up again in springs on the shore of Lake Ohrid.

teile.einleitung: The Riksdag is the parliament of Sweden. It makes the laws, decides the state budget and elects the prime minister. The Riksdag meets in Stockholm.
wichtigste: The Riksdag is the parliament of Sweden.
It has 349 seats.
It meets in Stockholm on the island of Helgeandsholmen.
Since 1971 the Riksdag has consisted of only one chamber.
The king has no political power, and the country is governed by parliament and the government.

abschnitte.text: The **Riksdag** has **349 seats**. It meets in **Stockholm** on the small island of **Helgeandsholmen** in the old town. The members are elected by the people every four years. A party needs at least 4 per cent of the votes to enter the Riksdag. This limit is called a **threshold**.

The Riksdag decides **laws** and the **state budget**, that is, what the state spends money on. It elects the **prime minister**, who leads the government. Sweden is a **monarchy** with a king, but the king has no political power. He represents the country mainly at ceremonial occasions. The decisions are made by parliament and government.

Since **1971** the Riksdag has consisted of only **one chamber**. Switzerland, by contrast, has a parliament with two chambers, the **Federal Assembly** with the National Council and the Council of States, 246 seats together. In Sweden the parliament elects the head of government. In Switzerland the Federal Assembly elects the seven members of the **Federal Council**.

gewusst: The word “Riksdag” means roughly “diet of the realm”, that is, assembly of the kingdom.
The roots of the Riksdag go back to the 15th century.

teile.einleitung: Europe consists of many states, from huge countries to tiny microstates. Exactly how many there are is disputed, because some states lie only partly in Europe. Switzerland lies in the middle of the continent.
wichtigste: The exact number of states is disputed, because some lie only partly in Europe.
Russia has the largest area of all countries with territory in Europe.
The Vatican is the smallest state in Europe and Monaco the second smallest.
France is the largest country in the EU by area.
Luxembourg is the only grand duchy in the world.
30 states belong to the EEA (as of 2025).

abschnitte.text: How many states belong to Europe is **disputed**. The reason: some countries lie only **partly in Europe**. Russia and Turkey, for example, have a large part of their territory in Asia. Depending on how you count, you arrive at about 45 to 50 states. **Russia** has the largest area of all countries with territory in Europe.

Europe has an especially large number of **microstates**. The smallest state in the world is the **Vatican**, in the middle of Rome. The second smallest is **Monaco** on the Mediterranean. **San Marino** lies entirely within Italy, but not in Rome. Other microstates are Andorra, Liechtenstein and **Luxembourg**, the only **grand duchy** in the world.

In the EU, **France** is the largest country by area. If you count only countries that lie entirely in Europe, **Germany** has the most inhabitants. In the far north-west lies the island state of **Iceland** in the North Atlantic, close to the Arctic Circle. Iceland belongs to Europe, although it is far from the mainland.

Many states work closely together. The **European Union** has 27 members (as of 2025). The **European Economic Area** (EEA) includes 30 states: the EU countries plus Norway, Iceland and Liechtenstein. **Switzerland** is in neither the EU nor the EEA. It manages its relations with the EU through treaties of its own, the so-called **bilateral agreements**.

The map of Europe has changed often. After the end of the Soviet Union and Yugoslavia, many new states came into being. **Czechoslovakia** was divided **peacefully** into two states in 1993: the **Czech Republic** and **Slovakia**. People therefore sometimes speak of a “velvet divorce”.

gewusst: The Vatican is so small that you can walk around it in less than an hour.
Liechtenstein and Uzbekistan are the only countries in the world that are surrounded only by landlocked countries.

teile.einleitung: Free movement of persons means that people from certain countries may live and work freely in another country. Between Switzerland and the EU it has applied since 2002 through an agreement.
wichtigste: The free movement of persons is one of the four fundamental freedoms of the EU single market.
The agreement on free movement between Switzerland and the EU has applied since 1 June 2002.
It is part of the Bilateral Agreements I, which are linked by the guillotine clause.
The accompanying measures have protected against wage dumping since 2004.
In 2020 the Swiss electorate rejected the Limitation Initiative with about 62 per cent No votes.
Cross-border commuters receive the G permit.

abschnitte.text: The EU **single market** rests on four freedoms: the free movement of **goods**, **persons**, **services** and **capital**. The free movement of persons includes the **free movement of workers**. Anyone who comes from one EU country may work in another EU country. After the eastward enlargement in 2004, the older EU states were allowed to restrict access for at most **seven years**.

Switzerland is not in the EU, but it has concluded **bilateral agreements**. The **Bilaterals I** were signed in 1999. The agreement on free movement came into force on **1 June 2002**. The seven agreements are linked by the **guillotine clause**: if Switzerland terminates one of them, the other six lapse as well.

The free movement of persons is often debated in Switzerland. Supporters stress that the economy needs skilled workers. Critics worry about immigration, housing and wages. In **2014** the Mass Immigration Initiative was narrowly accepted. On **27 September 2020** the people rejected the **Limitation Initiative**, which wanted to end free movement, with about **61.7 per cent** No votes.

Since **2004** there have been the **accompanying measures**. The cantons and the social partners, that is employers and trade unions, check whether foreign firms comply with Swiss **wage and working conditions**. This is meant to stop wages coming under pressure. People speak of protection against **wage dumping**.

Anyone who lives abroad and works in Switzerland receives the **G permit** as a **cross-border commuter**. As of 2024 the largest foreign group in Switzerland were **Italians**, ahead of Germans and Portuguese. With Brexit at the end of 2020, the **United Kingdom** ended free movement with the EU.

gewusst: Thanks to the agreement, Swiss people too may live and work in EU countries.
Cross-border commuters usually return to their place of residence at least once a week.

teile.einleitung: The Seine is one of the best-known rivers in France. It flows through the middle of Paris and runs into the English Channel. Many famous buildings stand on its banks.
wichtigste: The Seine is about 780 kilometres long.
It rises in the region of Burgundy.
It flows through Paris and Rouen.
It runs into the English Channel.
On the Île de la Cité stands the cathedral of Notre-Dame.
In 2024 the opening ceremony of the Olympic Games took place on the Seine.

abschnitte.text: The Seine **rises** in the region of **Burgundy** on a plateau, so quite far to the east of France. It is about **780 kilometres** long. It flows north-west in many loops. After Paris it reaches Normandy with the city of **Rouen**. At Le Havre it flows into the **English Channel**, the sea between France and England.

In **Paris** the Seine divides the city into a right bank and a left bank. Close to the river stand the **Eiffel Tower**, the Louvre museum and many other sights. Numerous bridges cross the Seine in Paris. The oldest one still standing is, of all things, called the **Pont Neuf**, which means “New Bridge”. Tour boats with visitors from all over the world sail on the river.

In the middle of Paris two islands lie in the Seine. On the **Île de la Cité** the history of the city began. The cathedral of **Notre-Dame** stands there. In 2019 it was badly damaged by a fire and was then painstakingly restored. Next to it lies the smaller Île Saint-Louis.

On the banks of the Seine, green wooden boxes stand along the walls. In them the **bouquinistes** sell old books, postcards and pictures. The riverbanks are a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**. In 2024 the **opening ceremony of the Olympic Games** was not held in a stadium but on the Seine: the athletes travelled along the river on boats.

gewusst: The Pont Neuf is called the “New Bridge”, although it is the oldest bridge in Paris.
The bouquinistes have been selling books on the Seine for centuries.

teile.einleitung: The Tiber is the river on which Rome lies. It is about 400 kilometres long, rises in the Apennines and runs into the Mediterranean. Many legends and buildings of the Romans are linked to it.
wichtigste: The Tiber flows through the middle of Rome, the capital of Italy.
In Italian it is called Tevere.
It is about 400 kilometres long and rises on Monte Fumaiolo in the Apennines.
It runs into the Tyrrhenian Sea, part of the Mediterranean, west of Rome.
At its mouth lay Ostia, the port of ancient Rome.
According to legend, Romulus and Remus were abandoned on the Tiber.

abschnitte.text: The **Tiber** is called **Tevere** in Italian, and the name Tiber comes from Latin. It rises on **Monte Fumaiolo** in the Apennines and flows south through central Italy. At about 405 kilometres, it is among the longest rivers in Italy. In the middle of **Rome** it winds through the city. West of Rome it runs into the **Tyrrhenian Sea**, a part of the Mediterranean.

abschnitte.titel: The legend of Romulus and Remus
abschnitte.text: An old legend tells of the twins **Romulus and Remus**. As babies they were left in a basket on the Tiber. The basket got stuck on the bank, and a **she-wolf** found the children and fed them with her milk. Later, according to the legend, Romulus founded the city of Rome. The she-wolf with the twins is still an emblem of the city today.

At the mouth of the Tiber lay the port city of **Ostia**. Its name comes from the Latin word “ostium” for mouth. Here ships arrived with grain and other goods for Rome. The goods were then taken on boats up the river into the city. You can visit the ruins of Ostia today.

On the bank of the Tiber stands the round **Castel Sant’Angelo**. It was built as a tomb for Emperor **Hadrian** and later converted into a fortress. In the middle of the river lies **Tiber Island**, the only island of the Tiber in Rome. It is small and shaped like a ship. Two old bridges connect it to the two banks, one of which dates from the time of the ancient Romans.

gewusst: The Ponte Fabricio to Tiber Island is more than 2,000 years old and is regarded as the oldest surviving bridge in Rome.
The name Ostia means roughly “mouth”.

teile.einleitung: Tulcea is a city in the east of Romania on the Danube. It is regarded as the “gateway to the Danube Delta”. Most boat trips into the large natural area start from here.
wichtigste: Tulcea lies in the east of Romania on the Danube.
The city is regarded as the “gateway to the Danube Delta”.
Most boat trips into the delta begin here.
The administration of the Danube Delta Biosphere Reserve is based in Tulcea.
The Danube Delta is an important habitat for birds and fish.

abschnitte.text: **Tulcea** lies where the Danube begins to divide into several arms shortly before the Black Sea. Because there are hardly any roads in the **Danube Delta**, people there often travel by boat. Most trips begin in Tulcea. That is why the city is called the **“gateway to the Danube Delta”**. Ships also leave from here for small places such as Sulina on the sea.

The Danube Delta is a huge area of reeds, lakes, channels and islands. It is a **biosphere reserve** and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. A biosphere reserve is an area in which nature is protected and people can still live and work. The administration of the reserve has its seat in Tulcea. Very many species of birds live in the delta, for example **pelicans**.

gewusst: Large colonies of pelicans live in the Danube Delta, which is rare in Europe.

teile.einleitung: Santorini, also called Thira, is a Greek island in the Aegean Sea. It was formed by a volcano and lies in a half circle around a huge crater filled by the sea. White houses and blue church domes have made it world famous.
wichtigste: Santorini was formed by a volcano.
The island lies around a large caldera, a collapsed basin filled by the sea.
Around 1600 BC there was a gigantic eruption, called the Minoan eruption.
The ancient city of Akrotiri was buried under ash.
The main town is called Fira, and Oia is famous for its sunsets.
Most houses are white, and many church domes are blue.

abschnitte.text: Santorini belongs to the **Cyclades** island group in Greece. The island was formed by a **volcano**. Around **1600 BC** it erupted with enormous force. This eruption is called the **Minoan eruption**, after the Minoan culture that was flourishing on Crete at the time. It is one of the largest volcanic eruptions of the last few thousand years.

After the eruption the middle of the volcano collapsed. This created a huge **collapsed basin** that filled with seawater. It is called a **caldera**, after the Spanish word for cauldron. Santorini lies like a half circle around this caldera, with steep cliffs facing the water. In the middle lie small dark volcanic islands, and the volcano has still not become extinct.

Before the eruption there was a rich city on the island called **Akrotiri**. About **3,600 years ago** it was buried under a thick layer of **ash**. Archaeologists have dug up houses with several storeys and colourful **wall paintings** there. Because hardly any human remains were found, it is assumed that the inhabitants managed to flee in time. Some people suspect that the story of Santorini influenced the legend of **Atlantis**.

The main town **Fira** lies high up on the edge of the caldera. Many steps lead up from the harbour, and you can climb them on foot, by cable car or on **donkeys**. Most houses are painted **white**, and many **church domes** are **blue**. The white keeps the houses cooler in the hot sun. In the village of **Oia**, many people watch the **sunset** every evening.

gewusst: The word caldera comes from Spanish and means cauldron.
Wall paintings more than 3,500 years old have survived in Akrotiri.

teile.einleitung: The Thames is the best-known river in England. It flows through Oxford and right through the middle of London and then runs into the North Sea. Many famous bridges and buildings stand on its banks.
wichtigste: The Thames is pronounced roughly “Temz”.
It is about 350 kilometres long, more precisely about 346 kilometres.
It is the longest river that lies entirely in England.
It rises in the Cotswolds and runs into the North Sea.
In London you can feel the ebb and flow of the tides.
The Thames Barrier protects London from storm surges.

abschnitte.text: The Thames rises in the **Cotswolds**, a hilly region in the west of England. The source is called **Thames Head** and lies in the county of Gloucestershire. From there the river flows east, passing through the university city of **Oxford** and Windsor Castle, among other places. At about 346 kilometres, the Thames is the longest river that lies entirely in England. East of London it becomes wider and wider and runs into the **North Sea**.

In **London** the Thames flows right through the city. Many famous buildings stand on its banks, such as Parliament with Big Ben and the Tower of London. Numerous bridges cross the river, including Tower Bridge. Because the sea is not far away, the water in London rises and falls every day with the **tides**. The difference can amount to several metres.

In strong storms the sea can push up the Thames. Then London is threatened by a **storm surge**. That is why the **Thames Barrier** was built east of the city. It is a large flood barrier with huge gates in the river. When there is danger, the gates are closed, and the seawater is kept out.

Since 1829 the universities of **Oxford and Cambridge** have held a famous rowing race, the **Boat Race**. Eights row against each other on the Thames in London. In the past it was so cold in some winters that the Thames froze over. Then Londoners held **fairs** with stalls and games on the ice. The last of these fairs took place in 1814.

gewusst: In Oxford the Thames is also called the “Isis”.
Today seals even live in the mouth of the Thames again.

teile.einleitung: The 1.5 degree target says that the Earth should, if possible, warm by no more than 1.5 degrees compared with the time before industrialisation. It is set out in the Paris climate agreement of 2015. Even half a degree more has big consequences for nature and people.
wichtigste: The Paris Agreement aims to hold warming well below 2 degrees and, if possible, limit it to 1.5 degrees.
In 2018 the IPCC published a special report on 1.5 degrees.
By 2030 CO2 emissions would have to fall by around 45 per cent compared with 2010.
Around 2050 CO2 emissions would have to reach net zero.
2024 was the first calendar year above 1.5 degrees.
The target refers to an average over around 20 years.

abschnitte.text: At the climate conference in **Paris** in 2015 the states agreed to hold warming well below **2 degrees** and, if possible, to limit it to **1.5 degrees**. The **Alliance of Small Island States** (AOSIS) pushed especially hard for it. These countries are under severe threat from rising sea levels. Their motto was “1.5 to stay alive”. Switzerland has also signed the agreement.

The conference asked the **Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC)** for a report. It appeared in October **2018**. According to it, CO2 emissions would have to fall by around **45 per cent** by **2030** compared with 2010. Around **2050** they would have to reach **net zero**. Net zero means that no more CO2 is emitted than is taken back out of the air. For 2 degrees that point would not come until around 2070.

abschnitte.titel: Every tenth of a degree counts
abschnitte.text: The report shows how much half a degree makes. At 1.5 degrees, 70 to 90 per cent of **warm-water coral reefs** disappear, at 2 degrees more than **99 per cent**. An **ice-free Arctic summer** would be expected about once per century at 1.5 degrees. At 2 degrees it would be about once per decade.

According to the **WMO** and **Copernicus**, **2024** was the first calendar year to lie more than 1.5 degrees above the pre-industrial level (as of 2025). That does not mean the target is automatically missed. It refers to long-term warming, that is, an **average over around 20 years**. Single years vary, for example because of the weather phenomenon **El Niño**.

Researchers calculate how much CO2 may still be emitted. This **CO2 budget** was estimated in early 2024 at around **200 gigatonnes**, for a 50 per cent chance of not exceeding 1.5 degrees. At around 40 gigatonnes a year it would be used up after about **5 years**. That is why acting quickly is seen as especially important.

gewusst: An ice-free summer in the Arctic would be about ten times as frequent at 2 degrees as at 1.5 degrees.
A gigatonne is a billion tonnes.

teile.einleitung: Vesuvius is a volcano in southern Italy on the Bay of Naples. It is famous for its eruption in AD 79, which buried the Roman cities of Pompeii and Herculaneum. It is still regarded as an active volcano today.
wichtigste: Vesuvius lies near Naples and is about 1,281 metres high.
In AD 79 it buried Pompeii and Herculaneum.
Pompeii was buried under ash and small stones.
Vesuvius is a stratovolcano made of lava and ash.
Its last eruption was in 1944.
Pliny the Younger described the eruption of 79 in letters.

abschnitte.text: Vesuvius is a **stratovolcano**, also called a **composite volcano**. It is built up of alternating layers of **lava** and **ash**. Its magma is thick and contains a lot of gas. That is why its eruptions are often **explosive**. At about 1,281 metres it is much smaller than the high mountains of the Alps, but very dangerous.

In **AD 79** Vesuvius erupted with enormous force. It spewed out huge amounts of ash and **pumice**, which fell on the city of **Pompeii** and buried it. **Herculaneum** at the foot of the mountain was also buried, as was the town of Stabiae. Only many centuries later did people begin to excavate the cities. Today they show how the Romans lived: houses, streets, bakeries and wall paintings have survived.

The Roman scholar and fleet commander **Pliny the Elder** set out with ships during the eruption to rescue people and to observe the volcano. He died on the coast near Stabiae. His nephew **Pliny the Younger** later described the eruption in two letters to the historian Tacitus. He told of a cloud that looked like a pine tree. Very explosive eruptions with a high column of ash are now called **Plinian** after him.

Vesuvius has erupted many times since then. The **last eruption** was in **1944**. Since then it has been quiet, but not extinct. Very many people live around the mountain. That is why the volcano is closely **monitored** by a research station, so that a warning can be given in time if there is danger. There are also plans for how the area would be evacuated in the event of a new eruption.

gewusst: The volcano observatory on Vesuvius was founded as early as the 19th century and is regarded as the oldest in the world.
The excavations of Pompeii are a UNESCO World Heritage Site and are visited by millions of people every year.

teile.einleitung: Šumadija is a hilly region in the heart of Serbia. Its name comes from the Serbian word for forest. It is regarded as the heartland of Serbia.
wichtigste: Šumadija lies in the middle of Serbia, south of Belgrade.
“Šuma” means forest in Serbian.
In the past the area was densely wooded.
The largest city is Kragujevac.
Šumadija is regarded as the heartland of Serbia.

abschnitte.text: The Serbian word **“šuma”** means forest. Šumadija was once covered with dense oak forests. Today there are many fields, orchards and vineyards on gentle **hills**. The area is also known for **plums**.

The largest city in Šumadija is **Kragujevac**. In the 19th century it was for a time the capital of Serbia. Another well-known place is **Topola**. The capital **Belgrade** lies on the northern edge of the region.

In Šumadija the **First Serbian Uprising** against Ottoman rule began in 1804. That is why the region is regarded as the cradle of modern Serbia. Many Serbs still see it as the **heartland** of their country.

gewusst: Although Šumadija means “wooded land”, a large part of the old forests has disappeared today.

teile.einleitung: Portugal lies at the far west of Europe on the Iberian Peninsula. The country has only one neighbour, Spain, and a long coast on the Atlantic. The capital is Lisbon.
wichtigste: Portugal borders only Spain, and otherwise the Atlantic.
The capital is Lisbon, and the second largest city is Porto.
Cabo da Roca is the westernmost point of mainland Europe.
Vasco da Gama found the sea route to India in 1498.
With the Carnation Revolution in 1974 Portugal became a democracy.
The Azores and Madeira in the Atlantic also belong to Portugal.

abschnitte.text: Portugal lies in the west of the **Iberian Peninsula**. In the north and east it borders **Spain**, and in the west and south the **Atlantic**. West of Lisbon near Sintra lies **Cabo da Roca**, the westernmost point of mainland Europe. Two island groups in the Atlantic also belong to Portugal: the **Azores** and **Madeira**. In the south lies the sunny **Algarve** with many beaches.

In the 15th and 16th centuries Portugal was one of the greatest sea powers in the world. Portuguese ships sailed further and further along the coast of Africa. In 1498 **Vasco da Gama** sailed round the Cape of Good Hope as far as **India**. This began trade with Asia, for example in spices. Portugal founded bases and colonies on several continents. That is why Portuguese is spoken today in Brazil, Angola and Mozambique as well.

For almost 50 years Portugal was a **dictatorship**, that is, a state in which people were not allowed to vote freely. On **25 April 1974** the military overthrew the government almost without bloodshed. People put **carnations** into the barrels of the soldiers' rifles. That is why this event is called the **Carnation Revolution**. After that Portugal became a democracy and in 1986 joined the European Community, today's EU.

The capital **Lisbon** lies at the mouth of the River Tagus. Old yellow trams run through its steep lanes. In 1755 the city was destroyed by a severe **earthquake** and then rebuilt. Lisbon is also known for **fado**, sad songs full of longing.

Many people from Portugal live in Switzerland. They are among the largest groups of foreign residents in the country. Many work, for example, in construction, in hotels or in care. So Portuguese specialities such as the sweet pastry **pastel de nata** are known in Switzerland too.

gewusst: The name Portugal comes from “Portus Cale”, the old name of the area around Porto.
The Vasco da Gama Bridge in Lisbon is over 17 kilometres long and one of the longest bridges in Europe.

teile.einleitung: Pizza is a flat dough with toppings that is baked in an oven. It comes from Naples in Italy and is now popular all over the world, including in Switzerland.
wichtigste: Pizza as we know it comes from Naples.
The dough consists mainly of flour, water, yeast and salt.
A pizza Margherita is topped with tomatoes, mozzarella and basil.
The pizza Margherita is named after a queen.
Genuine Neapolitan pizza is baked in a wood-fired oven.
The art of the pizzaiolo from Naples is part of UNESCO's cultural heritage.

abschnitte.text: Flat breads with toppings have existed for a long time. But **pizza** as we know it today was invented in **Naples** in southern Italy. There are still very many **pizzerias** there today. With the people who emigrated from Italy, pizza came to many countries. In Switzerland too it is among the most popular dishes.

The **pizza Margherita** is named after **Queen Margherita** of Italy. According to legend she was especially fond of this pizza. It is topped with **tomatoes**, white **mozzarella** and fresh **basil leaves**. Red, white and green are also the colours of the Italian flag. The **pizza Marinara** is even simpler: tomatoes, garlic, oregano and olive oil, but **no cheese**.

For **pizza dough** you only need **flour**, **water**, **yeast** and **salt**. The yeast makes the dough **rise**, so it becomes light and soft. Then it is pressed flat by hand and topped. In Naples the rim is thick and soft, and it is called the **cornicione**.

A genuine pizza from Naples goes into a very hot **wood-fired oven**. Inside it is over 400 degrees. This way the pizza is ready in about **a minute and a half**. The pizza baker is called a **pizzaiolo** in Italian. He makes the dough, tops the pizza and bakes it. The art of the **pizzaioli** from Naples is part of **UNESCO's cultural heritage**.

gewusst: The art of the Neapolitan pizzaiolo was recognised by UNESCO in 2017.
“Marinara” means roughly “sailor style”.

teile.einleitung: Very many different languages are spoken in Europe. Most of them are related to each other and belong to the large family of Indo-European languages. Switzerland alone has four national languages.
wichtigste: Most languages in Europe belong to the Indo-European languages.
Italian, French, Spanish and Portuguese are Romance languages.
The EU has 24 official languages (as of 2025).
Greek has its own script with letters such as α and β.
In Poland people speak Polish, in Sweden Swedish.
Switzerland has four national languages.

abschnitte.text: Most languages in Europe belong to the **Indo-European languages**. They descend from a very old common ancestor language. That is why some words are similar: the German word “Mutter” is “mother” in English and “mor” in Swedish. Within the family there are groups. The **Germanic** ones include German, English and Swedish, and the **Slavic** ones include Polish and Czech, for example.

The **Romance languages** developed from the Latin of the ancient Romans. They include **Italian**, French, Spanish, **Portuguese** and Romanian. Romansh in the Grisons also belongs to them. In Italian you say **“Grazie”** for thank you. In French you greet people with **“Bonjour”**, in Spanish with **“Hola”**.

Most languages in Europe are written in the **Latin alphabet**. **Greek**, however, has its own script with letters such as **α (alpha)** and **β (beta)**. The word “alphabet” comes from these two. Russian, Bulgarian and Serbian are written in the **Cyrillic** script, which developed from the Greek one.

The European Union has **24 official languages** (as of 2025). Important laws are translated into all of these languages. Not all languages in Europe are Indo-European: **Finnish**, Estonian and **Hungarian** belong to a different family. **Basque** in Spain and France is not related to any known language.

Switzerland has four **national languages**: German, French, Italian and Romansh. Many children learn a second national language at school, plus English. In everyday life in German-speaking Switzerland people mostly speak **Swiss German dialect**. In this way Switzerland shows in miniature how varied Europe is.

gewusst: The word “alphabet” is made up of the first two Greek letters, alpha and beta.
Hungarian and Finnish are distantly related, although the countries lie far apart.

teile.einleitung: Shkodra is a city in the north of Albania. It lies on the shore of Lake Skadar, the largest lake on the Balkan Peninsula, on the border with Montenegro. Shkodra is one of the oldest cities in the country.
wichtigste: Shkodra lies in the north of Albania.
The city lies on Lake Skadar on the border with Montenegro.
Shkodra is one of the oldest cities in Albania.
Rozafa Castle stands above the city.
In German the city is also called Skutari.

abschnitte.text: Shkodra lies on the south-eastern shore of **Lake Skadar**. It is the largest lake on the Balkan Peninsula. One part of the lake belongs to Albania, the other to **Montenegro**. The River Buna flows from the lake to the Adriatic Sea. The Drin also flows past nearby. In German the city is often called **Skutari**.

abschnitte.titel: An old city with a castle
abschnitte.text: Shkodra is one of the **oldest cities in Albania**. It was already an important place in ancient times. On a hill above the city stands **Rozafa Castle**. From there you can see far across the lake and the rivers. A well-known Albanian legend is woven around the castle.

Shkodra is regarded as an important **cultural centre** in the north of Albania. In the city, mosques and churches stand close together. Many people cycle here, because the area is flat. From Shkodra, travellers set off for the **Albanian Alps**, a wild high mountain range in the north of the country.

gewusst: Lake Skadar is the largest lake on the whole Balkan Peninsula.
Shkodra is one of the cities in Albania where particularly many people ride bicycles.

teile.einleitung: After Asia, Africa is the second-largest continent on Earth. Here there are huge deserts, dense rainforests, wide savannas and the longest river in the world, the Nile. Researchers agree that humankind originally comes from Africa.
wichtigste: At around 30 million square kilometres, Africa is the second-largest continent.
There are 54 states on the continent.
The highest mountain is Kilimanjaro in Tanzania at 5,895 metres.
The Nile flows through Egypt, where the pyramids of Giza stand.
Since 2011 Algeria has been the largest country in Africa by area.
Nigeria has the most inhabitants of all African countries.
Wild animals such as giraffes, elephants and lions live in Africa.
Lesotho is entirely surrounded by South Africa.

abschnitte.text: Africa lies south of Europe and is separated from it by the **Mediterranean** and the Strait of Gibraltar. In the west it borders the Atlantic, in the east the Indian Ocean. The **equator** runs through the middle of the continent, so it is warm all year round in large parts. Africa is about 700 times as big as Switzerland.

In the north lies the **Sahara**, the largest hot desert on Earth. In the middle, around the Congo Basin, dense rainforest grows. In between, and in the east and south, lie large **savannas** with grass and scattered trees. The highest mountain is **Kilimanjaro** in Tanzania, a volcano with snow on its summit even though it stands close to the equator.

At around 6,650 kilometres, the **Nile** is the longest river in Africa and is often regarded as the longest river in the world. It flows through Egypt into the Mediterranean. Other large rivers are the Congo, the Niger and the Zambezi, on which Victoria Falls lie. The largest lake is Lake Victoria in East Africa.

Africa is known for its large wild animals such as **giraffes**, elephants, lions, rhinoceroses and zebras. Many of them live in national parks such as the Serengeti in Tanzania. In the rainforest live gorillas and chimpanzees. On the island of Madagascar there are lemurs, which occur nowhere else in the world.

About 1.5 billion people live in Africa, as of 2024, and the population is growing fast. **Nigeria** has the most inhabitants, and **Algeria** has been the largest country by area since South Sudan became independent in 2011. Over a thousand different languages are spoken, and often English, French, Arabic or Portuguese as well. Many countries were colonies of European states for a long time and became independent only around 1960.

In East Africa the oldest traces of humans and their ancestors were found, which is why Africa is called the **cradle of humankind**. In ancient **Egypt** around 5,000 years ago one of the first advanced civilisations arose, with writing and pyramids. The pyramids of Giza are among the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World. Empires such as Aksum in Ethiopia or Mali were also once very powerful.

begriffe.erklaerung: A very large piece of land on Earth, for example Africa or Europe.
A wide grassland with scattered trees in warm regions.
An area that is ruled by a foreign state.
A state or territory that is entirely surrounded by the territory of another state, like Lesotho.

gewusst: Despite being close to the equator, Kilimanjaro has glaciers on its summit, but they are shrinking fast.
Lesotho lies so high that its lowest point is higher than the lowest point of any other country in the world.
The Sahara is about as big as the USA.

teile.einleitung: The Massif Central is a large, old mountain range in the middle and south of France. It is known for extinct volcanoes, green plateaus and famous cheese. It takes up about 15 per cent of the area of France.
wichtigste: The Massif Central is much older than the Alps.
The highest mountain is the Puy de Sancy at around 1,886 metres.
The Chaîne des Puys volcanic chain has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2018.
The Puy de Dôme lies near Clermont-Ferrand.
The Millau Viaduct spans the valley of the Tarn.
In the south the cheese Roquefort matures in caves.

abschnitte.text: The **Massif Central** was formed more than **300 million years ago**. It is much **older than the Alps** and has been heavily worn down over a long time. That is why it is lower and rounder than the rugged Alps. It covers around **85,000 square kilometres**, about **15 per cent** of the area of France. That is roughly twice the area of Switzerland. Important rivers such as the **Loire** rise here.

Much later, **volcanoes** formed in the Massif Central. The **Chaîne des Puys** consists of around 80 extinct volcanoes west of **Clermont-Ferrand**. It has been part of the **UNESCO World Heritage** since **2018**. Its landmark is the **Puy de Dôme**, at around 1,465 metres. Since 2012 a **rack railway**, the “Panoramique des Dômes”, has run to the summit. The highest mountain of the Massif Central is the **Puy de Sancy** at around 1,886 metres, also a former volcano.

The extinct **Cantal** is regarded as the **largest volcano in Europe** by area. It had a diameter of around 70 kilometres. Today it is heavily eroded. From its centre, valleys run outwards like the **spokes of a star**. Many cows graze on the green pastures of the region, and cheese is made.

In the south the **Millau Viaduct** crosses the valley of the **Tarn**. It opened in 2004 and is among the tallest bridges in the world. In the cool limestone caves of **Roquefort-sur-Soulzon** the blue cheese **Roquefort**, made from sheep’s milk, matures. In **Le Puy-en-Velay** the **Via Podiensis** begins, one of the most important French **Ways of St James** to Santiago de Compostela.

gewusst: The volcanoes of the Chaîne des Puys look like a row of green hills with craters on top.
Roquefort may only be called that if it has matured in the caves of Roquefort-sur-Soulzon.

teile.einleitung: Red Square is the most famous square in Moscow, the capital of Russia. It lies right beside the wall of the Kremlin. On the square stand the colourful St Basil's Cathedral and the large department store GUM.
wichtigste: Red Square lies in the centre of Moscow.
Right beside it stands the Kremlin with its red walls.
St Basil's Cathedral has colourful domes like onions.
The old Russian word for “red” also used to mean “beautiful”.
Opposite the Kremlin stands the department store GUM.
The square is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

abschnitte.text: In Russian the square is called **Krasnaya Ploshchad**. The word **“krasnaya”** today means “red”. In the past, however, it also meant **“beautiful”**. So the name really meant “the beautiful square”. Originally it had nothing to do with the red colour of the walls or with politics. The square is about 330 metres long.

On one side of the square stands the **Kremlin**. This is an old **fortress** with red brick walls and many towers. On some of the towers red stars shine. Behind the walls stand palaces and churches. Today the **president** and the government of Russia work in the Kremlin. That is why the word “Kremlin” often stands for the Russian government.

At the southern end of the square stands **St Basil's Cathedral**. It was built in the 16th century and is over 450 years old. Its **colourful domes** look like onions, so people speak of **onion domes**. Each dome has different colours and patterns. The church is a landmark of Moscow and of all Russia.

Opposite the Kremlin stands **GUM**, a large old department store. It was built at the end of the 19th century. Over its long arcades arches a large **glass roof**, so that a lot of daylight falls in. Today there are many shops and cafés there.

At the Kremlin stands **Lenin's Mausoleum**, a tomb for the revolutionary leader Lenin. On Red Square festivals, markets and large **parades** took place over the centuries. Since 1990 Red Square and the Kremlin have been a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**. In winter there is often an ice rink on the square.

gewusst: The name “Red Square” originally meant “beautiful square”.
St Basil's Cathedral actually consists of several churches built together.

teile.einleitung: The Sognefjord is the longest and deepest fjord in Norway. It reaches about 205 kilometres inland and is about 1,300 metres deep at its deepest point. Glaciers shaped it in the Ice Age.
wichtigste: The Sognefjord is about 205 kilometres long.
At its deepest point it is about 1,300 metres deep.
It lies in the county of Vestland (as of 2025).
A glacier carved out a valley, which the sea later flooded.
The side arm Nærøyfjord is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
The longest fjord in the world is Scoresby Sund in Greenland.

abschnitte.text: The **Sognefjord** lies on the west coast of Norway in the county (fylke) of **Vestland** (as of 2025). It is about **205 kilometres** long and so the longest fjord in Norway. At its deepest point it measures about **1,300 metres**. Steep mountains rise on the left and the right. Only the **Kangertittivaq**, also called Scoresby Sund, in Greenland is longer.

In the Ice Age a mighty **glacier** flowed through a river valley to the sea. It carved the valley deeper and deeper. This created a **trough valley** with a **U-shaped** cross-section. When the ice melted, the sea level rose, and the sea flooded the valley. At its **mouth** a fjord is usually shallower than inside. There is a **rock sill** there, because at this spot the glacier eroded less deeply, that is, it removed less rock.

To the north of the Sognefjord lies **Jostedalsbreen**. It is the largest glacier on the European mainland. Some glacier tongues reach down into the side valleys. The meltwater flows into the fjord in rivers and waterfalls.

abschnitte.titel: Side arms and the Flåm Railway
abschnitte.text: Many narrow **side arms** branch off from the Sognefjord. The **Nærøyfjord** is only about 250 metres wide in places. It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site **“West Norwegian Fjords”**. On the **Aurlandsfjord** lies the village of **Flåm**. The **Flåm Railway**, one of the steepest standard-gauge railway lines, ends there. It runs through tunnels and past waterfalls up into the mountains.

gewusst: The deepest point of the Sognefjord lies deeper below the sea than many mountains on its shore are high.
At its narrowest point the Nærøyfjord is only about 250 metres wide.

teile.einleitung: Trollstigen is a steep mountain pass road in Norway. It winds up a rock face in eleven tight hairpin bends. The name means “Troll’s Ladder” or “Troll’s Path”.
wichtigste: Trollstigen is a mountain pass road in the west of Norway.
It has eleven tight hairpin bends.
The road climbs a very steep rock face.
In winter it is closed because of snow.
At the top there is a viewing platform with a view into the valley.

abschnitte.titel: Eleven bends on the rock face
abschnitte.text: **Trollstigen** lies in the west of Norway between high mountains. The road winds up a steep rock face in **eleven hairpin bends**. A **hairpin bend** is such a tight curve that the road almost carries on in the opposite direction. Beside the road a waterfall plunges into the depths. The road was opened in the 1930s.

In winter a lot of snow lies there, and there is a danger of avalanches. That is why Trollstigen is usually open only from late spring to autumn. During this time many travellers drive up. At the top there is a **viewing platform** from which you look down into the valley and at the bends. The name recalls the **trolls**, legendary creatures that appear in many stories in Norway.

gewusst: Trollstigen is one of the particularly beautiful routes that Norway designates as National Tourist Routes.

teile.einleitung: Veliko Tarnovo is a town in the north of Bulgaria. In the Middle Ages it was the capital of the Second Bulgarian Empire. It is known for the fortress on Tsarevets Hill.
wichtigste: Veliko Tarnovo lies in the north of Bulgaria.
From 1185 to 1393 the town was the capital of the Second Bulgarian Empire.
The remains of the fortress stand on Tsarevets Hill.
The town lies on slopes above the River Yantra.
In 1393 the Ottomans conquered the town.

abschnitte.text: In **1185** the brothers **Asen** and **Peter** rose up against the Byzantine Empire. This is how the **Second Bulgarian Empire** came about. Its capital was **Veliko Tarnovo**, from 1185 to 1393. During this time the town was a centre for rulers, the Church and art. In **1393** the **Ottomans** conquered the town, and the empire came to an end.

The town lies on steep slopes above the **Yantra**, which winds in tight loops through the valley. On **Tsarevets** Hill stand the remains of the medieval **fortress**. This was once the site of the tsar’s palace and the patriarch’s church. The church was rebuilt and today stands at the top of the hill.

The town is also important for modern Bulgaria. In **1879** the first **constitution** of the new Bulgarian state was adopted here. Today Veliko Tarnovo has a **university** and a beautiful old town with old houses built on the slope.

gewusst: Because the houses stand so steeply on the slope, the old town looks as if the houses were climbing over one another.

teile.einleitung: Sulina is a small port town in Romania. It lies where the middle arm of the Danube flows into the Black Sea. Sulina is the easternmost town in Romania and can only be reached by ship.
wichtigste: Sulina lies at the mouth of the middle arm of the Danube on the Black Sea.
It is the easternmost town in Romania.
There is no road to Sulina, and you can only get there by ship.
The town lies in the middle of the Danube Delta, a large nature reserve.
The kilometre count of the Danube begins at its mouth at Sulina.

abschnitte.titel: A town at the end of the Danube
abschnitte.text: Shortly before the sea the Danube divides into three main arms. The middle one is called the **Sulina Arm**, and the town of Sulina lies at its end. Because there is no road there, visitors travel by ship, usually from the city of Tulcea. Around the town lies the **Danube Delta**, with reeds, lakes and many birds. It is a biosphere reserve and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

In the 19th century the Sulina Arm was widened and straightened so that larger ships could sail from the Danube to the sea. At that time Sulina was a lively port in which people from many countries lived. Today the town is small and quiet. An old **lighthouse** recalls the time when the sea was still closer to the town. Because the Danube brings a lot of sand and mud, the land at the mouth is slowly growing out into the sea.

gewusst: The kilometre markings along the Danube are counted upstream from the mouth at Sulina.

teile.einleitung: The Acasta Gneiss is one of the oldest known rocks on Earth. It lies in the north of Canada and is around 4 billion years old. Researchers learn a great deal from it about the young Earth.
wichtigste: The Acasta Gneiss is around 4 billion years old.
It lies in the Northwest Territories of Canada.
It belongs to the Canadian Shield, a very old part of the Earth’s crust.
Gneiss is a rock that has been transformed under great pressure and heat.

abschnitte.text: The **Acasta Gneiss** lies on the Acasta River in the **Northwest Territories** of Canada. It has been dated to around **4 billion years**. That makes it one of the oldest known rocks in the Earth’s crust. The Earth itself is about 4.6 billion years old. So the gneiss comes from a very early time in Earth’s history.

A **gneiss** is a **metamorphic rock**. That means an older rock was transformed deep in the Earth by great **pressure** and high **heat**. This often produces light and dark stripes. There is also a lot of gneiss in the Swiss Alps, but it is much younger there.

The Acasta Gneiss belongs to the **Canadian Shield**. This is the name for a huge area of very old rocks in North America. Such old cores of the continents are called **cratons**. Because they have been stable for a very long time, ancient rocks have been preserved there.

gewusst: Even older traces of the Earth are tiny zircon crystals from Australia, but as a whole rock the Acasta Gneiss is among the oldest.

teile.einleitung: Vojvodina is an autonomous province in the north of Serbia. It is very flat and fertile and is therefore called the breadbasket of Serbia. Its capital is Novi Sad on the Danube.
wichtigste: Vojvodina is an autonomous province in the north of Serbia.
It belongs to the flat Pannonian Plain.
Because of its fertile soils it is called the breadbasket of Serbia.
Its capital is Novi Sad on the Danube.
People with many different languages live in Vojvodina.

abschnitte.text: Vojvodina lies in the **Pannonian Plain**, a large, flat landscape. The soils are very **fertile**. That is why a lot of **wheat**, **maize** and **sunflowers** are grown there. The region is therefore called the **breadbasket of Serbia**. Large rivers such as the **Danube** and the **Tisza** flow through the area.

The capital of the province is **Novi Sad** on the Danube. After Belgrade it is the second-largest city in Serbia. On the other side of the river stands the large **Petrovaradin Fortress**. In the south of the city rises the hilly region of **Fruška Gora**, otherwise Vojvodina is flat almost everywhere.

Vojvodina is an **autonomous province**. That means it may decide some things itself, much as a canton in Switzerland decides some things itself. Besides Serbs, many **Hungarians**, Slovaks, Romanians and other groups live in the region. That is why there are several **official languages** there.

gewusst: In Vojvodina several languages are official at once, including Serbian, Hungarian and Slovak.

teile.einleitung: Aboriginal Australians are the first inhabitants of Australia. Their ancestors have lived on the continent for at least 50,000 years. That gives them one of the oldest cultures in the world.
wichtigste: Aboriginal Australians have lived in Australia for over 50,000 years.
In the past most of them lived as hunters and gatherers.
According to their stories, the world came into being in the Dreamtime.
The didgeridoo is their well-known wind instrument.
Many of their paintings are made up of small dots.
Before the arrival of Europeans there were over 250 languages.

abschnitte.text: In the past most Aboriginal Australians lived as **hunters and gatherers**. They hunted animals and gathered fruits, roots and seeds. In doing so they knew their land and its **waterholes** very well. That was vital in often dry Australia. Before the arrival of Europeans there were over **250 languages**, and today many of them are hardly spoken any more.

According to Aboriginal stories, **ancestral beings** shaped the land, the animals and the people in the **Dreamtime**. These stories have been handed down for a very long time. They explain how mountains, rivers and waterholes came about. Many places in the landscape are therefore regarded as sacred.

A very long time ago Aboriginal Australians painted pictures on **rock walls**. These **rock paintings** show animals, people and stories. **Dot painting** is also well known: pictures are made up of countless coloured dots. These too often tell old stories from the Dreamtime.

The **didgeridoo** is a long wind instrument made from a hollow branch, often hollowed out by **termites**. It sounds deep and droning, a little like an alphorn. The **Aboriginal flag** is black, red and yellow. Black stands for the people, red for the earth and the yellow circle for the sun. Today it is an official flag of Australia.

gewusst: The wood for a didgeridoo is often hollowed out not by people but by termites.
Aboriginal Australians belong to the oldest continuously existing cultures on Earth.

teile.einleitung: Saint Petersburg is the second-largest city in Russia and the largest city on the Baltic coast. It was founded more than 300 years ago by Tsar Peter the Great. With its canals, palaces and bridges, it is one of the most beautiful cities in Europe.
wichtigste: Saint Petersburg is the largest city on the Baltic coast.
Tsar Peter the Great founded the city in 1703.
The city lies at the mouth of the River Neva.
For about 200 years it was the capital of Russia.
In the time of the Soviet Union it was called Leningrad.
The Hermitage is one of the largest art museums in the world.

abschnitte.text: In **1703** Tsar **Peter the Great** founded the city at the mouth of the **Neva** where it flows into the Baltic Sea. He wanted to create a “window to Europe” and make Russia more modern. The city was built on marshy ground, which was very laborious. Just a few years later Peter made it the **capital** of Russia. It remained so until 1918, after which Moscow became the capital again.

Over time the city had three names. From 1914 it was called **Petrograd**, because the name was meant to sound more Russian. From 1924 it was called **Leningrad**, after the revolutionary leader Lenin. In the Second World War Leningrad was besieged for about 900 days, from 1941 to 1944, and very many people died of hunger and cold. Since **1991** the city has again borne its old name, **Saint Petersburg**.

The tsars used to live in the magnificent **Winter Palace**. Today it is part of the **Hermitage**, one of the largest art museums in the world. The Peter and Paul Fortress and many churches with golden domes are also well known. The historic city centre is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**. Outside the city there are large palace complexes with gardens and fountains.

Many **canals** run through Saint Petersburg, which is why it is also called the “Venice of the North”. Large bridges lead across the Neva, and at night they are **raised** so that ships can pass through. In early summer it hardly gets dark at all. This time is called the **white nights**. Then many people celebrate outdoors until late into the night.

gewusst: In Saint Petersburg, bridges are raised at night so that large ships can sail along the Neva.
In the 20th century the city had three different names.

teile.einleitung: Teide is a volcano on the Canary island of Tenerife. At about 3,715 metres it is the highest mountain in Spain. It stands in a national park that is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
wichtigste: Teide stands on the island of Tenerife, which belongs to the Canary Islands.
